title: Insight-dismiss write escapes the /api/finance admin gate (role bypass)
evidence: financeRoutes.mjs:1530  app.put("/api/insights/:id/dismiss", requireAuth, async (req, res) => { ... sb.from("cost_intelligence_insights").update({ is_dismissed: true, dismissed_by: req.caller?.id ... }).eq("id", req.params.id) ... }  — This is the ONLY route registered by the finance files that is not under the /api/finance path. The admin gate in dev-api.mjs:835-846 only loops over prefixes ["/api/finance", "/api/sales", ...]; "/api/insights" is absent. requireAuth (requireAuth.mjs:24-25) blocks only role==="client"; it does NOT check role, so any active employee or supervisor token passes. Every sibling finance route is admin-only via the prefix gate, but this one inherits only requireAuth.
repro: As a non-admin staff member (role 'employee' or 'supervisor'), obtain a valid Supabase session token, then: curl -X PUT https://<host>/api/insights/<any-insight-uuid>/dismiss -H 'Authorization: Bearer <employee_jwt>'. The cost-intelligence insight is silently dismissed (is_dismissed=true) despite the entire Financial Command Centre / Cost Intelligence surface being Director(admin)-only by design. Frontend caller is JobCommandCentre.jsx:659 (authFetch PUT /api/insights/:id/dismiss), an admin-only page, but the endpoint is independently reachable.
impact: A supervisor or employee can suppress Director-only financial/cost-intelligence alerts (margin erosion, underclaim risk, budget overrun flags) that they are not authorised to see or act on, hiding them from the admin's Command Centre feed. Same class of gap the team already fixed for /api/carpentry (dev-api.mjs:848-851: "READ endpoints were requireAuth-only, letting any authenticated employee/client curl ... data"). Not exploitable by unauth or client roles (requireAuth blocks both), and the write is low-stakes (toggles an advisory flag, no money/contract mutation), hence medium not high. The handler also violates two project laws: it returns { error: msg } without ok:false (lines 1532,1534,1543) and leaks raw error.message (translateDbError not used).
fixSketch: Add "/api/insights" to the prefix gate loop in dev-api.mjs:835 (or wrap the route with requireRole("admin")), matching every other finance surface. While editing, convert the responses to ok()/err() from apiResponse.mjs and run error.message through translateDbError so raw Postgres strings don't reach the browser.

title: Variation create/edit uses bare fetch() — no auth token, every save 401s
repro: Open a job's Command Centre → Variations tab (JobCommandCentre.jsx:801 mounts this component) → click 'New variation', fill title + amount → 'Create variation'. The request goes out with no Authorization header → requireAuth returns 401 → j.ok is false → UI shows 'Failed to save' (or the generic error). Editing a draft variation (PUT) fails identically. Creating/editing via authFetch works, so this is specific to the save path.
impact: Variations cannot be created or edited from the live Variations component at all — a completely broken core money workflow (variations feed signed-variation totals → canonical contract_value → all downstream claim %/margin math).
fixSketch: Replace `fetch(url, …)` on line 247 with `authFetch(url, …)` (authFetch is already imported at the top of the file).

title: WIPAA panel calls a renamed/nonexistent endpoint — 404, panel never populates
evidence:
const r = await authFetch(`/api/finance/jobs/${jobId}/wipaa`).then(r => r.json());
There is no GET /api/finance/jobs/:id/wipaa route. The WIPAA endpoint was moved/renamed to GET /api/finance/jobs/:jobId/wipaa/current (financeCCRoutes.mjs:801); financeRoutes.mjs:1113 even leaves a comment 'WIPAA: served by GET /api/finance/jobs/:jobId/wipaa/current'. Express will not match /wipaa to /wipaa/current. JobFinancials.jsx predates the rename (git log: file last touched in older commits; wipaa/current introduced 2026-05-21 'Financial Command Centre — data integrity'). Additionally the panel reads wipaa.invoice_count (line 139) and wipaa.progress_billed (line 160), but /wipaa/current returns neither (it returns cost_to_date, pct_complete, earned_revenue, wipaa, projected_margin_pct, … — financeCCRoutes.mjs:840-851).
repro: Finance Manager → 'Jobs' tab (FinanceManager.jsx:126 mounts <JobFinancials/>) → pick a project. WipaaPanel.load() hits /api/finance/jobs/<id>/wipaa → 404 JSON → r.ok falsy → setWipaa never called → the 'Calculating…'/empty state persists; WIPAA position, % complete, earned revenue never show. Even if the URL were corrected, invoice_count renders as 'undefined invoices' and 'Progress billed' shows '—'.
impact: The standalone WIPAA calculator (APB monthly over/under-billing position — a money-management feature) is dead for every job. Director cannot see earned-revenue vs progress-billed from this page.
fixSketch: Point the fetch at `/api/finance/jobs/${jobId}/wipaa/current`. Then either add invoice_count + progress_billed to the /wipaa/current response, or stop reading those fields in the panel (derive progress_billed from claims if needed). Verify the response key (r.wipaa) matches.

title: KPI mismatch: 'Claims paid' is inc-GST cash but 'Claims issued' is ex-GST — paid shows ~110% of issued
evidence:
command-centre handler:
  const claimsIssued = claims.filter(c => c.status !== "draft").reduce((s, c) => s + Number(c.amount_ex_gst || 0), 0);   // EX-GST
  const claimsPaid   = claims.reduce((s, c) => (c.progress_claim_payments||[]).reduce((ps,p)=>ps+Number(p.payment_amount||0),0)…  // payment_amount
Payments are recorded INC-GST: the pay modal labels the field 'Amount received (inc GST)' (ProgressClaims.jsx:283) and defaults it to `amount_ex_gst * 1.1 - amount_paid` (ProgressClaims.jsx:251); the pay route confirms paid-in-full by comparing totalPaid against `amount_ex_gst * 1.1` (financeCCRoutes.mjs:1364). So payment_amount is inc-GST. Same mismatch in /summary (claimsIssued line 363 ex-GST vs claimsPaid line 370 payment_amount) and /portfolio/kpi-summary (lines 472 vs 476).
repro: Create a $10,000 ex-GST claim, issue it, record full payment ($11,000 inc-GST as the modal pre-fills). Command Centre shows Claims issued = $10,000 and Claims paid = $11,000 (JobCommandCentre.jsx:627-628 render them as adjacent KpiCards). A fully-paid job displays 'paid' exceeding 'issued' by the GST, implying client overpaid.
impact: Director-facing KPI cards are internally inconsistent (one ex-GST, one inc-GST) on every job with recorded payments; 'Claims paid' overstates collection by 10% relative to 'Claims issued', and cumulative comparisons (issued vs paid gap) are wrong. Mirrored to the client portal claimsPaid (ClientHome.jsx:125).
fixSketch: Pick one basis for the pair. Simplest: report claims_paid on an ex-GST basis by dividing payment sums by (1+GST_RATE), or store/track payment_amount ex-GST. Alternatively present BOTH KPIs inc-GST (claims_issued = amount_inc_gst). Use the generated amount_inc_gst column / exGst() helper rather than ad-hoc division.

title: Payment status uses hardcoded *1.1 GST and contradicts how payment_amount is read everywhere else (ex-GST vs inc-GST)
repro: Create a claim with amount_ex_gst = 10000 (inc GST = 11000). Record payment_amount = 10000 (the operator pays the ex-GST figure, OR the system treats payments as ex-GST as it does everywhere else). /pay computes claimAmount = 11000; totalPaid (10000) < 11000*0.99 → status stays 'partially_paid' even though the claim is effectively settled in the ledger the rest of the app uses. Conversely, in /summary (line 368-370) and /command-centre (line 643) and /cashflow (line 2261 `unpaid = amount_ex_gst - paid`), the SAME payment_amount of 10000 is subtracted from the ex-GST claim of 10000 → cashflow shows unpaid = 0 / fully paid, while the claim row says partially_paid. The two views permanently disagree.
impact: Two defects in one: (1) violates the project money law (CLAUDE.md: never hardcode *1.1, use incGst()/GST_RATE). (2) payment_amount has no single agreed GST basis — /pay treats it as inc-GST to set claim.status, but cashflow, claims_paid KPI and the claim list's amount_paid all treat it as ex-GST. Claims will get stuck in partially_paid (clogging the overdue/requires-action lists) or the Director KPI 'claims_paid' will be ~9% off vs the actual settled status. Real cash reconciliation is wrong.
fixSketch: Decide one basis for payment_amount (cash received = inc-GST is the natural one) and apply it consistently. In /pay import incGst from constants and use claimAmount = incGst(claim.amount_ex_gst); then make claims_paid/cashflow convert (compare paid inc-GST against incGst(amount_ex_gst)) OR store payments ex-GST and drop the *1.1 here. Either way remove the literal 1.1 and unify the GST basis across /pay, /summary, /command-centre and /cashflow.

title: Payment can be recorded against a draft (never-issued) claim
repro: POST /api/finance/jobs/:jobId/claims to create a claim (status defaults to 'draft', never sent to client). Immediately POST .../claims/:claimId/pay with payment_amount = full inc-GST amount. The guard only rejects 'void'/'disputed', so the payment inserts and the claim jumps draft → paid without ever being issued. syncClaimPaid then mirrors a 'paid' state to the client portal for an invoice the client was never sent.
impact: Lets a claim be marked paid that was never issued — corrupts claims_issued vs claims_paid relationship (a paid claim that is excluded from claims_issued only when status==='draft' in /command-centre line 641, yet here a paid claim is no longer draft, so it now counts as issued retroactively with no issued_date). Portal/My-Actions can show a paid invoice with no underlying issued document.
fixSketch: Restrict /pay to claims in an issued-family status: if (!["issued","overdue","partially_paid","paid"].includes(claim.status)) return err(res,400,"Only an issued claim can record a payment"). Mirror the explicit allow-list the WIPAA snapshot already uses.

title: Void and Dispute have no status precondition — a paid claim can be voided, a void claim re-disputed
repro: Record a full payment on a claim (status → 'paid', cash banked, payments rows exist). Then POST .../void with any reason. The row flips to 'void' unconditionally. Now /summary excludes it from claims (it filters .neq('status','void')), so claims_issued silently drops by this claim's amount while the payment rows still exist (payments are summed from progress_claim_payments without re-checking claim status in /summary line 368). Result: claims_paid > claims_issued, an impossible ledger. Equally, a 'void' claim can be POSTed to /dispute and become 'disputed' again, un-voiding it.
impact: Voiding a paid/partially-paid claim orphans its recorded payments and produces claims_paid exceeding claims_issued in the Director KPI bar; the cancelled-cash money trail is lost. No guard prevents nonsensical transitions (paid→void, void→disputed, disputed→disputed).
fixSketch: Add precondition checks: void should refuse claims with any recorded payments (or only allow draft/issued/overdue/disputed without payments); dispute should require status IN ('issued','overdue','partially_paid'). Read current status (already partially done for /pay) and reject illegal source states with err(res,400,...).

title: Variation sign is a non-atomic check-then-write → concurrent double-sign double-counts variation_amount in normalized_costs
repro: Fire two POSTs to .../variations/:vid/sign simultaneously while status is 'sent_to_client'. Both reads return 'sent_to_client' (the read at 2015 and the update at 2022 are separate statements; the UPDATE filters only on id, not on status). Both pass the guard, both run the UPDATE (idempotent at the row level), and both call upsertNormalizedCost with field:'variation' — which is ADDITIVE (normalizedCosts.mjs:76-77 `patch.variation_amount = prev + amount`). The variation's value is added twice to normalized_costs.variation_amount and thus to final_amount.
impact: Double-counts the variation's cost in the per-trade normalized cost ledger (final_amount, budget_vs_actual_pct, charge-up rates). contract_value itself is safe (recomputed from status='signed' rows), but the cost side inflates. Also affects any retry/double-click on Sign.
fixSketch: Make the transition atomic and idempotent: scope the UPDATE with the source status — .update({status:'signed',...}).eq('id',vid).eq('status','sent_to_client').select().maybeSingle(); if no row returned, treat as already-signed and skip the additive normalized-cost write. This guarantees exactly-once application even under concurrency.

title: AI job-matching tier references undefined identifier MODEL — every AI-tier match silently fails
repro: Upload (or poll) an invoice whose address/supplier doesn't hit any deterministic Tier 1/1b/1c/2 match, so execution reaches Tier 3 (line 259-294). Evaluating `model: MODEL` throws `ReferenceError: MODEL is not defined`. The whole Tier-3 block is wrapped in `try { ... } catch { /* AI tier failed — fall through to unmatched */ }` (line 291), so the error is swallowed and matchDocument returns { job_id: null, match_confidence: 0 } → the document is filed as 'unmatched'.
impact: The most sophisticated matching tier is dead code: it can NEVER succeed because it throws before the API call. Invoices that only the AI tier could place always land in the unmatched bucket, forcing manual re-matching. Lint/build pass (it's a runtime ReferenceError inside try/catch), exactly the class of bug the brief calls out. grep confirms no MODEL import or const anywhere in the file.
fixSketch: Change `model: MODEL` to `model: MODEL_SLOW` (Sonnet — the appropriate tier for ambiguous matching). Optionally add a unit/smoke test that forces the Tier-3 path.

title: Common estimate category names map to no workforce task → labour actuals silently $0
evidence: matchTaskCategory only matches against WORKFORCE_LABOUR_TASKS labels via `n === tn || n.startsWith(tn) || n.includes(tn)`. Tested: "Framing"→null, "Frame"→null, "First Fix"→null, "Labour"→null, "Carpentry Labour"→null, "Decking"→null. The seed stores `workforce_task_category: costType === 'labour' ? matchTaskCategory(name) : null` (1326); the budget GET then computes `actual = isLabour ? round2(labourByTask[b.workforce_task_category] || 0) : ...` (1398) — a null key reads `labourByTask[null]` = 0.
repro: Import a Buildexact estimate whose labour category is named "Framing" (or "First Fix", "Labour", "Carpentry Labour", "Decking"). Seed budget. Workers book approved timesheet hours under task_category first_fix_framing. Open Budget tab: the "Framing" line shows Budget = $X, Actual = $0, full variance — even though real labour was spent. labourActual total and burn-rate margin are understated by that amount.
impact: Margin/variance and the burn-rate guardrail are wrong (over-optimistic) for any job whose estimate uses category names that don't literally contain the canonical labels. The only signal is a generic amber warning (CarpentryJobDetail.jsx:1689-1690) that fires only when workforce_task_category is null AND someone reads it — the dollar figures themselves look authoritative and wrong. Buildexact category names are free-text and rarely match the 8 hardcoded labels exactly, so this is the common case, not an edge case.
fixSketch: Don't silently store null. At seed time, surface unmapped labour lines to the user for explicit mapping (the UI already half-does this via the dropdown at CarpentryJobDetail.jsx:1026 but only for already-mapped lines). Add an explicit alias table / fuzzy map covering frame/framing→first_fix_framing, fix→second_fix, decking/eaves→outdoor_works, labour→site_labouring, and persist a user override. Also fold the timesheet 'other' bucket somewhere instead of dropping it.

title: Two budget lines mapping to the same workforce_task_category double-count labour actuals
evidence: Each labour line independently reads the same bucket: `const actual = isLabour ? round2(labourByTask[b.workforce_task_category] || 0) : ...` (1397-1398), and the total is `labourActual = sum((l)=>l.costType==='labour',(l)=>l.actual)` (1416). Nothing dedups by task_category. matchTaskCategory maps both "Supervision" and "Site Supervision" → supervision (verified), so two distinct estimate categories can carry the same workforce_task_category.
repro: Estimate has two labour categories "Supervision" and "Site Supervision" (both → supervision). Approved timesheets book $5,000 under task_category 'supervision'. Budget tab: BOTH lines show Actual = $5,000, and totals.labourActual includes $10,000 — double the real $5,000. burn.labourMarginRemaining (1434) is correspondingly understated.
impact: Labour actual and remaining-margin are inflated 2x (or Nx) for the affected category whenever the estimate splits a single workforce stream across multiple named lines — a normal estimating habit. Directly corrupts the money figures the owner uses to judge job profitability.
fixSketch: Allocate each task_category bucket to exactly one line (e.g. distribute proportionally to budget, or pick the highest-budget line and zero the rest), or aggregate budget lines by workforce_task_category before computing actuals so a bucket is consumed once. Validate at seed time that no two labour lines share a workforce_task_category.

title: /budget, /summary and /closeout compute labour actuals from different cost bases and scopes — same job shows different numbers
evidence: Budget GET sums approved timesheet_entries.cost_amount (the loaded break-even rate written at approval, workforceRoutes.mjs:427-431) and ONLY over task_categories that have a matching budget line (1397-1398, 1416). Summary GET instead recomputes `labourActual += hours * Number(emp?.hourly_rate||0)` (1469-1471) over ALL approved timesheets regardless of category. Closeout does the same hourly_rate recompute (1553-1556). So three endpoints, two different per-hour cost bases (cost_amount/loaded-rate vs employees.hourly_rate) and two different scopes (mapped-lines-only vs all).
repro: Job with loaded cost model synced (cost_amount != hourly_rate) and one labour category that fails to map (see finding 1). Costing tab (summary, CarpentryJobDetail.jsx:1439) shows labourActual = all-hours × hourly_rate; Budget tab (1633) shows a smaller labourActual = mapped-only × loaded-rate. The two tabs of the same job disagree; the persisted carpentry_job_performance.final_labour_cost (closeout) is a third number.
impact: User cannot trust which labour-cost figure is correct; forecast margin (summary, surfaced as the headline % at lines 93/1419) and final margin (closeout, written to performance history) are computed on a base that ignores the synced loaded rate, while the Budget tab uses it. The historical performance snapshot used for future estimating is on the wrong (pay-rate, not loaded-cost) basis.
fixSketch: Pick one canonical labour-actual function (sum approved cost_amount, falling back to hours×loadedRate when cost_amount is null) and reuse it in /summary, /budget and /closeout. Don't recompute from employees.hourly_rate in summary/closeout when a loaded cost model exists.

title: Budget re-seed upsert key (cost_type,category_name) diverges from DB UNIQUE(job_id,category_name) → 500 on cost_type flip
evidence: Seed dedups with `keyOf = (r) => `${r.cost_type}:${category_name.lower()}`` (1335) and only UPDATEs when that composite key matches an existing row (1342-1347); otherwise it INSERTs (1349). But the table enforces `UNIQUE (job_id, category_name)` (067:19) — cost_type is NOT part of the DB key. If a re-import classifies an existing category_name under a different cost_type (e.g. a name that previously matched classifyCostType as material now resolves to labour, or the client passes an explicit costType), existingByKey misses the old row, the code attempts an INSERT with the same (job_id, category_name), and Postgres rejects it.
repro: Seed budget with category "Cladding supply and install" (classified once). Re-seed where the same category_name resolves to the other cost_type (e.g. user-edited costType, or a parser change). The INSERT at 1349 hits UNIQUE(job_id, category_name) → error → `return err(res, 500, translateDbError(error))` and the re-seed aborts partway, having already updated/inserted earlier categories — leaving the budget half-migrated.
impact: Re-import fails with a 500 and a partially-rewritten budget; the comment at 1331-1334 claims the upsert 'preserves cost FKs' but the keying is inconsistent with the DB constraint, so the safety it promises (keep ids, preserve carpentry_job_budget_id) breaks exactly when cost_type changes.
fixSketch: Key the upsert on (job_id, category_name) to match the DB UNIQUE, and update cost_type in place. Or change the constraint to UNIQUE(job_id, cost_type, category_name) and keep the current keyOf — but then update the comment. Either way, run the whole seed in a transaction so a failure doesn't leave a half-migrated budget.

title: Labour booked under timesheet task_category 'other' is dropped from per-category budget actuals
evidence: timesheet_entries.task_category CHECK allows 'other' (059:48-52: '...supervision','other'), but WORKFORCE_LABOUR_TASKS (1273-1282) has no 'other' entry, so no budget line can ever carry workforce_task_category='other'. Budget GET builds `labourByTask['other']` from those entries (1381) but no line reads it, so it never appears in any line.actual nor in labourActual (1416).
repro: Worker logs hours under task_category 'other' on a carpentry job; timesheet approved. Budget tab labourActual omits that cost entirely (it lands in labourByTask['other'] which no line consumes). Note /summary by contrast DOES count it (it sums all hours×rate), compounding finding 3's discrepancy.
impact: Any labour that doesn't fit the 8 named streams silently vanishes from the per-category budget view and the budget-tab labour total, understating spend and overstating remaining margin.
fixSketch: Either disallow 'other' for carpentry timesheets, or add an uncategorised/'other' budget bucket and surface labourByTask keys that no line consumes as an 'unallocated labour' row so the money is never silently lost.

title: Auto-layout adds calendar days, not working days — milestones land on weekends despite 'working days' model
evidence: Header comment: 'a build duration (working days at BASELINE_CREW)'. addDaysYmd(ymd, days){ const d=new Date(`${...}T12:00:00Z`); d.setUTCDate(d.getUTCDate()+Math.round(days)); ...}  — and in the layout loop: `const advance = Math.max(rule.leadDays, scaledBuild); target = addDaysYmd(cursor, advance);`  Nothing skips Sat/Sun or AU public holidays.
repro: node: autoLayoutMilestones({ commencementDate:'2026-07-10' /*Friday*/, milestones:[{id:1,name:'Frame start',sort_order:1},{id:2,name:'Frame complete',sort_order:2}] }) → Frame start = 2026-07-11 (Saturday), Frame complete = 2026-07-17. A crew cannot 'start framing' on a Saturday; every downstream target is also pulled off the working calendar and Queensland public holidays (e.g. Ekka, Christmas shutdown) are ignored entirely.
impact: Generated milestone target dates routinely fall on non-working days, so the proposed schedule is wrong by 1-2+ days per phase and drifts further as offsets accumulate. Supervisors get framing/lock-up/handover dates on weekends; the durations are systematically understated because a '10 working day' frame is laid out as 10 (scaled 6) calendar days spanning weekends. This is the core value of the feature and it is materially incorrect.
fixSketch: Advance by business days: implement addWorkingDaysYmd that increments day-by-day skipping getUTCDay() 0/6 (and a QLD holiday set), and apply it to scaledBuild. Keep leadDays as calendar days (procurement lead time is calendar). Then advance = the later of (cursor+leadDays calendar) and (cursor+scaledBuild working days). Optionally snap any pinned/anchor date forward to the next working day.

title: Frame-delivery anchor earlier than commencement produces a non-monotonic, nonsensical schedule
evidence: if (frameDeliveryDate && /frame delivery/i.test(m.name)) { target = frameDeliveryDate; } ... if (target && (!cursor || target > cursor)) cursor = target; else if (target) cursor = cursor; out.push({ id, name, targetDate: target });  — a pinned frame-delivery date is written to the milestone verbatim and the 'never go backwards' guard only protects the cursor, not the emitted targetDate.
repro: node: autoLayoutMilestones({ commencementDate:'2026-07-06', frameDeliveryDate:'2026-06-01', milestones:[Material ordered, Frame delivery, Frame start, ...] }) → Material ordered=2026-07-06, Frame delivery=2026-06-01 (BEFORE material is ordered and 5 weeks before commencement), Frame start=2026-07-07. The schedule is out of order: the frame is 'delivered' before it is ordered and before the job starts.
impact: A user who fat-fingers the frame-delivery date (or whose actual delivery slipped to a past date) gets a saved schedule where the delivery milestone precedes ordering/commencement. No validation rejects it; with apply:true these bad dates are persisted to carpentry_job_milestones. Downstream sorting/Gantt rendering and 'is X late?' logic key off these target_dates.
fixSketch: Validate frameDeliveryDate >= commencementDate (and ideally >= the prior milestone's target) in autoLayoutMilestones or the route; reject with err(res,400,...) or clamp the pinned date to the cursor and surface a warning in the preview rather than silently emitting an out-of-order date.

title: Zero-advance terminal milestones (Practical completion / handover) collide on the same date as their predecessor
evidence: { match: /practical completion|^complete$|handover/i, buildDays: 0, leadDays: 0, crew: null }. With buildDays 0 and leadDays 0, scaledBuild=0 → advance=Math.max(0,0)=0 → target = addDaysYmd(cursor, 0) = cursor unchanged.
repro: node: standard 11-milestone list, commence 2026-07-06 → Final inspection=2026-09-28 AND Practical completion=2026-09-28 (identical). Handover is scheduled for the same day the certifier inspection target lands, with no gap for the inspection to pass / certificate to issue.
impact: Practical Completion / handover always equals the date of the preceding milestone, so the proposed schedule shows the job finishing the same day as final inspection — unrealistic and confusing for client-facing handover dates. Any 'duration between final inspection and PC' is zero.
fixSketch: Give terminal milestones a minimum 1-working-day advance, or make any milestone with advance===0 still move the cursor forward by 1 working day so successive milestones never share a date; alternatively set buildDays:1 for the practical-completion rule.

title: Estimate-Items per-category SELL ex-GST understates supplier-direct / PC-PS lines (budget != client total)
evidence: Line 480-486 comment: "subtotal_sell_ex_gst = the marked-up sell price ex-GST (cost + markup) = inc-markup+tax − tax". But the code computes `const sell = Math.round((c.subtotal_ex_gst + c.subtotal_markup) * 100) / 100;` — i.e. cost + summed Markup column, NOT inc_gst − tax. Earlier at line 454-457 the same file explicitly states the scenario it must handle: "supplier-direct / client-supplied lines have cost 0 but a real sell price". For such a line, `Total`(cost)=0 and the `Markup` cell is blank/0, so `subtotal_markup` does not grow, yet `subtotal_inc_gst` (from TotalIncMarkupAndTax) does. `sell = cost + markup` therefore omits that line's sell price entirely.
repro: Simulated a category = one normal line (Total=1000, Markup=200, Tax=120, Inc=1320) + one PC/supplier-direct line (Total=0, Markup blank, Tax=50, TotalIncMarkupAndTax=550 → sell-ex-GST=500). Code path: subtotal_ex_gst=1000, subtotal_markup=200 → sell = 1200. Comment-intended sell (inc_gst − tax) = 1870 − 170 = 1700. The PC line's $500 sell is dropped. This `sell` becomes subtotal_sell_ex_gst → flows to /parse-xlsx `sellExGst` → /budget/seed `budget_ex_gst`, and into sell_total_ex_gst → carpentry_jobs.quoted_value. The client-facing estimate_total (inc GST) is correct, so the budget/quoted value is internally inconsistent with the GST-inclusive total.
impact: Carpentry budget_ex_gst and the job's quoted_value understate revenue by the full ex-GST sell of every cost-0 / PC / PS / supplier-direct line — exactly the lines the code claims to preserve. Budget-vs-actual variance and margin are wrong; the job looks less profitable / over budget than reality.
fixSketch: Compute sell as the comment intends: `const sell = Math.round((c.subtotal_inc_gst - c.subtotal_tax) * 100) / 100;` (inc-markup+tax minus tax). Keep subtotal_markup for reporting but derive sell from inc_gst − tax so PC/supplier-direct uplift is included. Then markup_amount/percent should also derive from this sell, not the Markup column sum.

title: Legacy report XLSX import and API fetch set quoted_value to COST (net_total), silently dropping markup
evidence: parse-xlsx handler: `const sellTotal = round2(p.sell_total_ex_gst ?? p.net_total);` and `quotedValue: sellTotal`. The report path of parseXLSX (buildexactParser.mjs:636-651) returns NO `sell_total_ex_gst` field and per-category objects with only `subtotal_ex_gst` (the AK column = pre-markup cost) — see lines 588-590 and 644-651. `net_total` is the Buildxact "Net Total" (pre-markup cost; confirmed because estimate_total falls back to `net_total + markup_amount + tax` at parser line 571). So for a report-format file, `sell_total_ex_gst` is undefined → quotedValue = net_total = bare cost. The API path (normaliseBuildexactEstimatePayload, parser:807) hardcodes `markup_amount: 0` and emits no sell, so /buildexact/fetch quotedValue (`estimate.sell_total_ex_gst ?? estimate.net_total`, routes:624) is likewise cost.
repro: Import a 'Categories & Items' (report) export instead of 'Estimate Items', or use Step-1 Fetch quotedValue. Estimate net cost $100k + 20% markup → Buildxact net_total=100000, markup=20000. Hub stores quoted_value=100000 (cost) and the per-category budget lines sum to 100000, while the real sell ex-GST is 120000. The budget banner and quoted value are understated by the entire $20k markup.
impact: On the legacy/report path and the API fetch path the carpentry job value and budget are the contractor's cost with zero margin — a 15-25% understatement of project value. The UI does steer users to Estimate Items, but report files still parse silently to a wrong number with no warning surfaced to the user beyond the sourceFormat string.
fixSketch: When source_format !== 'estimateitems' and there is markup_amount/markup_percent at estimate level, distribute markup pro-rata across categories to produce subtotal_sell_ex_gst, OR block the report format with an explicit error ("Use the Estimate Items export") rather than silently importing cost as the sell price. At minimum, set sell_total_ex_gst = net_total + markup_amount for the report path.

title: quoted_cost never populated from the XLSX import, so margin display is blank/wrong
evidence: parse-xlsx returns `raw.costTotalExGst = round2(p.net_total)` (carpentryRoutes.mjs:695) — the ex-markup cost — but handleXlsxFile (CarpentryDashboard.jsx:132-139) only sets `quotedValue: p.quotedValue` and never sets `quotedCost`. handleBxFetch (lines 100-110) also never sets quotedCost. The create payload (line 156) sends `quotedCost: form.quotedCost ? Number(form.quotedCost) : undefined`, so quoted_cost stays null unless typed manually.
repro: Import an Estimate Items XLSX, click through New Job. carpentry_jobs.quoted_value = sell, quoted_cost = null. Any margin = (value − cost)/value computed downstream reads cost as null/0 → margin shows 100% or NaN despite the cost being available in the parsed file.
impact: Margin/profitability for every imported carpentry job is missing or wrong out of the box; the cost figure the parser already extracted is thrown away, forcing manual re-entry that staff will skip.
fixSketch: In handleXlsxFile set `quotedCost: data?.raw?.costTotalExGst != null ? String(data.raw.costTotalExGst) : f.quotedCost` (and optionally derive quotedMarginPct). The server already returns it; just wire it into setForm.

title: GST hardcoded as *1.1 in parser (report + API + PDF paths) — violates GST_RATE law and drifts from constants.js
evidence: Report path: `const subtotal_inc_gst = Math.round(subtotal_ex_gst * 1.1 * 100) / 100;` (line 590). API normalise path: `cat.subtotal_inc_gst += Math.round(total * 1.1 * 100) / 100;` (line 773). PDF path: `cat.subtotal_inc_gst = Math.round(st * 1.1 * 100) / 100;` (line 698). Project law (CLAUDE.md / constants.js): "Never hardcode 0.1 or *1.1 — use GST_RATE/incGst()/gstAmount()". Note the report path *also* contradicts itself: it overwrites these *1.1 values with a markup+GST ratio at lines 629-633, making the line-590 computation dead but still a law violation and a maintenance trap.
repro: Static: grep `* 1.1` in buildexactParser.mjs returns 3 hits, none importing GST_RATE. If GST_RATE ever changes (or to centralise), these silently stay 10%.
impact: Category inc-GST shown to users on the API/PDF import paths is computed off a magic constant divorced from the single source of truth; a GST-rate change would leave carpentry imports wrong while the rest of the app updates.
fixSketch: Import GST_RATE/incGst from a shared server-side constants module (or mirror constants.js server-side) and replace each `* 1.1` with `incGst(x)`; delete the now-dead line-590 computation in the report path since it is overwritten by the ratio loop.

title: Worker PWA leaks supervisor/QC tasks — task_audience is never filtered server-side (D3 regression)
evidence: GET /api/worker/tasks builds the query with no task_audience predicate: `let q = sb.from("site_tasks").select("*, employees!assigned_to(id, name)").neq("status", "wont_do"); ... if (category) q = q.eq("category", category);` then `const visible = (tasks || []).filter(t => t.status === "done" || t.assigned_to === null || t.assigned_to === emp.id);`. There is no `t.task_audience !== "supervisor"` filter anywhere. grep confirms `task_audience` appears ONLY in carpentryRoutes.mjs (write) and CarpentryJobDetail.jsx (admin view) — never in workforceRoutes.mjs, WorkerTasks.jsx, or any RLS policy (mig 115 adds only the column + CHECK, no policy).
repro: 1) Admin/supervisor opens a carpentry job → Tasks → '+ Add Task', sets 'For: Supervisor (QC / order-ahead)', leaves assignee = 'Anyone on site', adds e.g. 'Order flashings ahead of cladding' (task_audience='supervisor', assigned_to=null). 2) A site worker opens the Worker PWA → Site tasks → picks that job. GET /api/worker/tasks returns the supervisor task (status open, assigned_to null passes the visibility filter). 3) It renders in the worker's Urgent/Normal list and the worker can tap 'Mark as done' → POST /api/worker/tasks/:id/complete succeeds (that endpoint also checks only assignment, not audience, workforceRoutes.mjs:1461-1466).
impact: The entire point of migration 115 + the admin 'Tasks for supervisors' section is to keep order-ahead/QC/inspection-booking tasks off the field crew's list. Because no API honours task_audience, every unassigned supervisor task shows up as a worker to-do (and order-ahead/QC tasks are typically unassigned). Workers see and can prematurely tick off procurement/QC items (e.g. mark 'Book frame inspection' done), corrupting the supervisor workflow and the job's QC trail. The admin UI's split is purely cosmetic on the office side and provides no actual segregation on the field side.
fixSketch: Add audience scoping to GET /api/worker/tasks: default to worker tasks only — `q = q.or('task_audience.is.null,task_audience.eq.worker')` (is.null guards rows created before mig 115 is applied). Mirror the same predicate in POST /api/worker/tasks/:id/complete's update filter so a worker cannot complete a supervisor task. Optionally expose audience to the supervisor-role field view if supervisors should see both.

title: site_tasks write/read endpoints leak raw Postgres errors and bypass apiResponse/camelCase laws
evidence: Multiple site_tasks handlers return raw DB error strings and bypass ok()/err(): e.g. POST /api/projects/:id/site-tasks: `if (error) return res.status(500).json({ ok: false, error: error.message });` (line 955) with `category: category || "general"` passed through unvalidated (line 950) — so an out-of-range category hits the DB CHECK and surfaces the raw Postgres constraint string. Same pattern at the bulk insert (976), GET project site-tasks (935), GET /api/worker/tasks (1394), and POST complete (1465: `error.message`). Project task inserts also never set task_audience and aren't validated against the category CHECK in app code, relying entirely on the DB to reject.
repro: POST /api/projects/:id/site-tasks with body {title:'x', category:'bogus'} → DB CHECK site_tasks_category_check rejects → response body is `{ok:false, error:"new row for relation \"site_tasks\" violates check constraint \"site_tasks_category_check\""}` reaching the browser. Project Standards Law: 'Never leak raw Postgres errors (use translateDbError)'.
impact: Raw Postgres constraint/column text reaches the client (information disclosure + ugly UX), and these endpoints violate the apiResponse.mjs contract the rest of the app relies on. Unvalidated category passthrough means input validation is delegated to the DB, producing 500s instead of clean 400s. Note the carpentry tasks routes (carpentryRoutes.mjs) correctly use err()/translateDbError — it is the workforce/project site_tasks routes that regressed.
fixSketch: Route all these handlers through err(res, status, translateDbError(error)) and ok(res, {...}); validate category against the shared whitelist before insert and return err(res,400,...) on miss; convert outputs via rowsToCamel so the frontend isn't forced to read snake_case (task.assigned_to / task.task_audience) as it does today.

title: Labour endpoint leaks per-worker and per-category labour cost ($) to non-director roles
evidence: GET /api/projects/:id/labour is gated by requireAuth only (line 852) and /api/projects is NOT in the admin prefix list (dev-api.mjs:835-846). It computes `isDirector = req.caller.role === 'admin'` (line 855) and correctly nulls the grand total: `total_cost: isDirector ? totalCost : null` (line 912). BUT it returns the per-category and per-worker cost unconditionally: byCategory accumulates `byCategory[cat].total_cost += Number(e.cost_amount || 0)` (line 873) and is returned as `entries_by_category: Object.values(byCategory)` (line 909); workerMap accumulates `workerMap[emp.id].cost += Number(e.cost_amount||0)` (line 892) and is returned as `workers_this_week: Object.values(workerMap)` (line 910) — each object still carrying `.cost`. So the response body delivers every worker's labour cost and each cost category's $ to the caller.
repro: Log in as a 'supervisor' or 'employee' (both non-director; roles.js viewCostData=admin-only). The Operations module is accessible to both (can.accessOperations). Open an Operations project, expand the Labour tab (OperationsProjectDetail.jsx:193 calls the endpoint via authFetch with the caller's own token), then inspect the Network response (or curl `/api/projects/<id>/labour` with the supervisor JWT). `entries_by_category[].total_cost` and `workers_this_week[].cost` are populated with real dollar amounts even though `total_cost` is null.
impact: Pay-cost confidentiality breach. Supervisors are explicitly supposed to get a cost-stripped view (roles.js: 'Supervisors get a cost-stripped view (build days/scope, not dollars)'). The UI happens not to render these fields today, but the server is the security boundary and ships the data; anyone with a non-admin staff token can read every site's labour cost and back out individual pay rates (cost ÷ hours per worker). This is exactly the cost-stripped-role leak the project laws prohibit.
fixSketch: Strip cost from the per-category and per-worker structures for non-directors, mirroring the total: when !isDirector, omit/zero `total_cost` on each entries_by_category row and drop `.cost` from each workers_this_week entry (e.g. map to {name, hours} only). Build the cost fields only inside an `if (isDirector)` branch.

title: All /api/workforce timesheet read endpoints are requireAuth-only — any employee can enumerate the whole workforce's timesheets
evidence: GET /api/workforce/timesheets/pending (line 624) and GET /api/workforce/timesheets (line 638) use only `requireAuth` (no requireRole), and the `/api/workforce` prefix is absent from the admin gate loop in dev-api.mjs:835-846. They return every employee's timesheets with employees(name, trade), projects, carpentry_jobs and timesheet_entries. Pay rate is correctly gated (`isDirector = req.caller.role === 'admin'` controls whether hourly_rate/overtime_multiplier are selected, lines 628-631/640-643), but hours/dates/projects of all staff are returned to any authenticated non-client caller. The role model (roles.js: accessWorkforce = admin+supervisor only; employee = 'site-only') intends employees to have no Workforce access at all.
repro: Obtain an 'employee'-role staff JWT (employees do log in — getDefaultRoute('employee') routes to /operations). `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <employee jwt>' /api/workforce/timesheets` returns ok:true with the entire company's timesheet history. The frontend hides the Workforce nav from employees, but the API does not enforce it.
impact: An ordinary site employee can read all colleagues' worked hours, which sites they were on, and submission/approval status — data they should not see per the documented role model. Lower than the cost leak because pay $ is stripped, but it is still an unintended cross-staff data exposure that the frontend role gate falsely implies is enforced.
fixSketch: Add `requireRole('admin','supervisor')` to the /pending, /timesheets, /completion-snapshot-adjacent and export.csv read endpoints (supervisor gets hours, admin also gets $ via the existing isDirector check), or add '/api/workforce' to the prefix gate with a supervisor-inclusive variant. Decide deliberately whether employees should reach any /api/workforce route at all.

title: Worker log-hours job picker is unscoped — leaks full project/carpentry portfolio + client names to any magic-link holder and allows hour attribution to arbitrary jobs
evidence: GET /api/worker/jobs (line 1206) correctly scopes via workerVisibleJobs() (active jobs + jobs the worker logged in the last 90 days). But GET /api/worker/projects (line 1128, still used by WorkerLogHours.jsx:70) returns the ENTIRE table unconditionally: `sb.from('projects').select('id, address, job_id, status')` and `sb.from('carpentry_jobs').select('id, address, client_name, status')` with no per-worker filter (lines 1135-1136), including client names baked into the carpentry address label (line 1144). Correspondingly POST /api/worker/timesheets (line 1225) accepts `project_id`/`carpentry_job_id` straight from the body (lines 1230, 1256-1259) with NO workerMaySeeJob() / workerVisibleJobs() check — unlike GET /api/worker/tasks which does authorise (lines 1379-1380).
repro: Hold any single worker magic-link token. `curl '/api/worker/projects?token=<tok>'` returns every project and every carpentry job (with client names) in the business, not just the worker's sites. Then POST /api/worker/timesheets with any project_id/carpentry_job_id UUID from that list (or guessed) — the timesheet is created and attributed to a job the worker has no relationship to.
impact: Privacy: a leaked or shared worker link discloses the whole client/site portfolio. Integrity: hours can be attributed to the wrong job (and that cost later flows to Buildexact actuals on approval), and a worker can self-attribute to jobs outside their visible set. Mitigated by admin approval before cost is booked, hence medium not high, but it contradicts the deliberate scoping the codebase added in workerVisibleJobs.
fixSketch: Point WorkerLogHours.jsx at /api/worker/jobs (the scoped source) and either retire /api/worker/projects or rewrite it to return workerVisibleJobs(). In POST /api/worker/timesheets, validate the supplied project_id/carpentry_job_id with workerMaySeeJob(await workerVisibleJobs(sb, emp.id), id, type) before insert, returning 403 otherwise.

title: Overtime/double-time computed PER TASK-ENTRY, not per day — multi-task days are systematically underpaid and labour actuals under-booked
evidence: approveSingleTimesheet loops entries and bands each one alone: `for (const entry of entries || []) { const bands = splitOvertimeHours(Number(entry.hours), settings...); const cost = computeCost(bands, ts.employees, loadedRate(...)); ... }`. splitOvertimeHours (line 47) applies overtime_threshold/double_time_threshold to a SINGLE entry's hours. A timesheet has one row per task_category (mig 059: timesheet_entries one per task within a day), so a 12h day logged as two task categories is two 6h entries — each 6h < 8h threshold → all regular, zero overtime/double-time.
repro: Worker logs a 12h day as 6h first_fix_framing + 6h cladding (the WorkerLogHours UI explicitly supports multiple task tiles per day). Settings overtime_threshold=8, double_time_threshold=10; employee rate $50, OT x1.5, DT x2.0. Per-entry: 2 × (6h regular × $50) = $600. Correct per-day (12h: 8 reg + 2 OT + 2 DT) = 8×50 + 2×75 + 2×100 = $750. Underpay $150/day. A 10h split 5+5 underpays $50/day. The same wrong (low) figure is booked to the carpentry/construction job as the labour actual via syncTimesheetToBuildexact (cost_amount → BX Work Order totalCost), so margin looks better than reality.
impact: Wrong money in two places: (1) overtime_hours and cost_amount under-state worker pay/cost whenever a day spans more than one task category and total hours cross the OT/DT threshold — a common case (framing in the morning, cladding in the afternoon); (2) the under-stated cost is the actual pushed to Buildexact, so job labour actuals and margin are overstated. A worker doing one task all day (single entry) is paid correctly, so the bug is silent and intermittent — exactly the class that escapes review.
fixSketch: Compute bands on the DAY total once, then allocate cost across entries pro-rata by hours. e.g. sum hours across entries, call splitOvertimeHours(dayTotal, settings) once, compute dayCost, then set each entry.cost_amount = round(dayCost * entry.hours / dayTotal, 2) (distribute the rounding remainder to the last entry so the sum reconciles). Likewise derive each entry's overtime_hours from the day-level split.

title: mass-fill always INSERTs entries without clearing existing ones — re-running (or filling a day already logged) duplicates hours and doubles labour cost
evidence: POST /api/workforce/timesheets/mass-fill finds-or-creates the timesheet (`let { data: ts } = await sb.from('timesheets').select('id').eq('employee_id', employee_id).eq('date', date).maybeSingle(); if (!ts) { ...insert... }`) then UNCONDITIONALLY `await sb.from('timesheet_entries').insert({...})`. There is no delete of prior entries. Contrast the worker path POST /api/worker/timesheets (line 1276) which does `await sb.from('timesheet_entries').delete().eq('timesheet_id', timesheetId)` before inserting on resubmit.
repro: Admin/supervisor uses Mass Fill for Mon for employee X (8h site_labouring) → 1 entry, 8h. They run Mass Fill again for the same Mon/employee (correct a typo, or the request retries) → a SECOND 8h site_labouring entry is appended to the same timesheet (UNIQUE(employee_id,date) on timesheets is satisfied — only the parent is unique; entries have no uniqueness). Day now shows 16h; on approval cost_amount is computed and booked for 16h. Also affects a day the worker already logged: mass-fill reuses that timesheet and appends on top of the worker's entries.
impact: Double-counted hours → double-counted pay and double-booked labour actuals to the job. Silent: no error, status flips to submitted, totals just inflate. Money wrong on both pay and job-cost sides.
fixSketch: Before inserting, delete existing entries for that timesheet on the first touch of each (employee,date) in the batch (mirroring the worker resubmit path), or upsert per (timesheet_id, task_category). Also guard against filling a timesheet that is already 'approved' (mass-fill currently reuses an approved timesheet's id and appends, with no status check).

title: No rate snapshot: cost is (re)computed from the CURRENT pay rate on every approval, so a later rate change retroactively rewrites the cost of any approved-but-not-yet-completed timesheet
evidence: Cost is always derived live: `const cost = computeCost(bands, ts.employees, loadedRate(cm, ts.employee_id));` reading the current employees.hourly_rate (joined as ts.employees) / current company_cost_model rate. There is NO rate_at_approval / rate_snapshot column anywhere (grep of server/ src/ supabase/ returns nothing). unapprove (line 819) nulls cost_amount, and re-approve recomputes at whatever the rate is THEN.
repro: Timesheet for week 1 approved at rate $50 → cost_amount booked. Buildexact sync is on manual mode (workforce_settings.buildexact_sync_mode != 'auto') or fails, so buildexact_completed_at is still null. Admin raises the employee's hourly_rate to $60 (PUT /employees/:id). Director un-approves + re-approves the old week (or sync-pending re-runs through approval) → week-1 cost silently recomputed at $60. The figure that flows to payroll/CSV export and to Buildexact actuals no longer reflects the rate in force during week 1.
impact: Historical labour cost/actuals are not stable against pay-rate edits until a Buildexact order completes (which is the only thing that freezes them). Reported job margin and any pay reconciliation off the cost_amount can shift retroactively. Lower severity because the common auto-sync path completes the BX order immediately on approval, freezing that side — but the Hub's own cost_amount and CSV export remain mutable.
fixSketch: Snapshot the effective rate (and multipliers) used at approval into a new timesheet_entries.rate_at_approval column and compute/recompute cost from the snapshot, not the live employee row; or stamp it once on first approval and never recompute on re-approval unless the entries' hours actually changed.

title: Leading-hand completion photos stored as raw base64 in the DB — violates the migration-099 path-only design
evidence: WorkerLogHours has its OWN inline compressor: `function compressImageToDataUrl(file...)` returning `canvas.toDataURL("image/jpeg", quality)` (lines 8-29). The photo picker stores that data URL straight into the entry: `patchEntry(idx, { completion_photo_url: await compressImageToDataUrl(file) });` (line 178). submit() then ships it verbatim: `completion_photo_url: e.completion_photo_url || null` (line 194). The server POST /api/worker/timesheets inserts it with no validation: `completion_photo_url: e.completion_photo_url || null` (workforceRoutes.mjs:1288). But siteMedia.mjs:1-7 states the column 'holds the object PATH only — never base64, never a URL', migration 099 confirms `completion_photo_url already exists ... (path string, NOT base64)`, and isValidPhotoKey (siteMedia.mjs:48-53) — which IS enforced on the site_task path — is never called here.
repro: 1. Open the PWA as a leading-hand worker. 2. Log hours → tap ⋯ on an entry → 'Add completion photo' → pick a photo. 3. Submit. The timesheet_entries.completion_photo_url row now contains a ~100-400KB `data:image/jpeg;base64,…` string instead of a `timesheet-entries/<id>/<date>-…` storage key. Contrast: WorkerTasks.jsx uses uploadWorkerPhoto() → /api/worker/photos → returns a storage path. Only LogHours was never migrated.
impact: Direct violation of the Canonical/storage law ('never base64 in the DB'). Every leading-hand timesheet photo bloats the timesheets payload: /api/worker/me and /api/worker/timesheets/:date select completion_photo_url, so home + prefill responses balloon with inline base64 over field cellular connections. signSiteTaskPhotos skips data: values (isStoragePath returns false on /^data:/), so these never go through the intended signed-URL path and are stored unencrypted-at-rest-policy-bypassing inline blobs. Office-side timesheet views that expect a signed URL field get a divergent shape.
fixSketch: Replace WorkerLogHours' inline compressImageToDataUrl + direct assignment with the shared uploadWorkerPhoto(file, { entityType: 'timesheet_entry', entityId }) helper (already supports timesheet_entry per PHOTO_ENTITY_DIR) so it stores a path, exactly like WorkerTasks. Server-side: in POST/PUT /api/worker/timesheets reject any completion_photo_url that fails isValidPhotoKey (mirror the /tasks/:id/complete guard) so base64 can never be persisted again.

title: Timesheet 'Site' picker lists every project + carpentry job to any worker, and the POST accepts any project id (unscoped)
evidence: WorkerLogHours populates the Site <select> from `/api/worker/projects` (effect at lines 66-82, rendered at :288-300). That endpoint runs `sb.from('projects').select('id, address, job_id, status')` and `carpentry_jobs.select('id, address, client_name, status')` with NO filter by the worker's visible set (workforceRoutes.mjs:1134-1137) — it returns ALL rows. This is unlike the carefully-scoped /api/worker/jobs (workerVisibleJobs, lines 1172-1223) whose own comment warns 'a UUID-valid jobId must still be checked against this set or any worker could enumerate every job'. The timesheet POST (1230-1294) only checks date and presence of project_id/carpentry_job_id — it never authorizes the id against workerVisibleJobs.
repro: Open the PWA as any active worker, go to Log hours, open the Site dropdown → every company project address and every carpentry job's address+client name is listed. Selecting any of them and submitting writes a timesheet against that arbitrary job id; the server accepts it.
impact: Info leak: a field worker sees the full list of project addresses and carpentry client names (RLS-equivalent leak, since worker endpoints run with the service role and bypass RLS). Integrity: a worker can log hours against a project they have no relationship to, polluting labour/cost attribution for that job.
fixSketch: Back the Site picker with the same workerVisibleJobs set used by /api/worker/jobs (or reuse /api/worker/jobs directly), and in POST/PUT /api/worker/timesheets validate project_id/carpentry_job_id against workerMaySeeJob(vis, id, type) before insert, returning 403 otherwise.

title: Ripple cascade has no cycle guard — cyclic dependencies cause a runaway loop (client) / server crash (server)
evidence: previewRipple re-enqueues any successor whenever `if (!task.start_date || task.start_date < requiredStart)` — there is no visited/updated Set and no cycle detection. With A depends-on B (FS) and B depends-on A (FS), each pass pushes the other forward, so the queue never drains. The server twin ripplePreview (scheduleRoutes.mjs:203-222) is structurally identical: `if (!t.start_date || t.start_date < requiredStart) { ... queue.push(t.id); }`. Note cascadeScheduleForward (the writer, line 332) DOES guard with `const updated = new Set([root.id])`, but ripplePreview and previewRipple do not.
repro: Node harness: tasks=[{id:'A',start:'2026-01-01',dur:2,task_dependencies:[{taskId:'B',type:'FS'}]},{id:'B',start:'2026-01-01',dur:2,task_dependencies:[{taskId:'A',type:'FS'}]}]; previewRipple(tasks,'A','2026-02-01'). Observed: ran ~2.5s, produced 1,456,206 affected rows, only stopping when dates overflowed into Invalid Date. The server ripplePreview uses addDaysYmd (throws on Invalid date) so the same input returns HTTP 502 instead of looping. The UI (TaskDetailPanel.jsx:211) only blocks direct self-dependency (`t.id !== task.id`); A→B + B→A is fully creatable.
impact: A user who creates a circular dependency (easy: two tasks each listing the other) then drags either task freezes the browser tab (1M+ iterations, multi-second hang on a 2-node graph; worse on larger graphs) or, on the server ripple-check, gets an opaque 502. No malice required — circular deps are a normal user mistake.
fixSketch: Add a per-task visited/updated Set gate to both previewRipple and the server ripplePreview exactly like cascadeScheduleForward already does, OR run a cycle-detect (DFS) before cascading and reject/break the cycle. Also have TaskDetailPanel reject a dependency that would create a cycle.

title: DB cascade + ripple-preview + reminders ignore typed task_dependencies (SS/FF/lag) — Sprint-3 typed deps are dead on the apply path
evidence: Both server-side cascades read ONLY legacy depends_on: ripplePreview line 208 `if (!(t.depends_on || []).includes(cid)) continue;` and line 209-211 compute `requiredStart = addDaysYmd(predEnds.sort().at(-1), 1)` — hardcoded FS+1, no type, no lag. cascadeScheduleForward line 339 `const deps = t.depends_on || []` likewise. Meanwhile TaskDetailPanel.jsx:213 writes ONLY task_dependencies (`patch({ task_dependencies: [...] })`) and never populates depends_on; the PATCH handler (scheduleRoutes.mjs:1029,1055) stores depends_on and task_dependencies as independent fields with no backfill. The correct typed math (getConstraint with SS/FF/lag) lives only in src/lib/scheduleUtils.js previewRipple, which ScheduleManager.jsx:555 invokes ONLY in the catch() fallback when the network fetch throws.
repro: In TaskDetailPanel add a dependency B→A of type SS lag=2 (no legacy depends_on). Drag A in the Gantt → ScheduleManager.onGanttDateChange calls POST /ripple-check → server ripplePreview sees B has empty depends_on → returns downstream_tasks:[] → no modal → optimistic PATCH → cascadeScheduleForward also sees empty depends_on → B is NOT moved. The SS+2 relationship the user declared has zero effect. (If a stale legacy depends_on also exists, B moves by FS+1 regardless of the declared FF/SS/lag.)
impact: The entire Sprint-3 typed-dependency feature (FS/SS/FF + lag) does not drive the actual schedule on save. Users build a typed dependency network, drag a predecessor, and successors either don't move or move with wrong (FS+1, lag-ignored) dates — silently, with the RippleWarningModal showing a count derived from the wrong engine. Wrong schedule dates flow to trade notifications and procurement order-by.
fixSketch: Make the server cascades dependency-type aware: port getConstraint (SS/FF/lag handling from scheduleUtils.js) into ripplePreview and cascadeScheduleForward, iterating `task_dependencies` (falling back to depends_on as FS+0) exactly like the client previewRipple. Alternatively, on PATCH, derive depends_on from task_dependencies so at least the predecessor set is complete — but that still loses type/lag, so porting the typed math is the real fix.

title: Procurement lead-time notifications hardcode 3 weeks for AI-generated tasks (lead_time_weeks null, real value in lead_time_days)
evidence: runLeadTimeNotifications selects only lead_time_weeks (line 130) and computes `const lead = task.lead_time_weeks != null ? Number(task.lead_time_weeks) : 3; const notificationDate = addDaysToIso(task.start_date, -(lead*7));`. But the AI generator buildRowsFromClaudePlan (scheduleGenerate.mjs:364-365) explicitly writes `lead_time_weeks: null, lead_time_days: procurement_lead_days` and stores the true lead in procurement_lead_days/lead_time_days. The reminders module never reads lead_time_days or procurement_lead_days.
repro: AI generates a 'Window order placed' procurement task with lead_time_days=98 (14 weeks, per canonical reference in scheduleClaudePlan.mjs:67) → row persisted with lead_time_weeks=null, lead_time_days=98. Lead-time cron: lead = (null != null ? ... : 3) = 3 weeks → notifies the supplier only 21 days before window install instead of ~98 days. The 14-week-lead item is ordered ~11 weeks too late.
impact: Long-lead items (windows, joinery, steel, trusses) — exactly the ones flagged as critical-path risks in the AI prompt — get their order/notification at a flat 3 weeks, guaranteeing late orders, missed install dates and schedule slip on the items most likely to control the critical path. Money + schedule correctness.
fixSketch: In runLeadTimeNotifications, select lead_time_days and procurement_lead_days too, and compute lead days as `Number(task.lead_time_days ?? task.procurement_lead_days) || (task.lead_time_weeks != null ? task.lead_time_weeks*7 : 21)`, then offset by that many days (not *7). Keep the 3-week fallback only when no lead field is set.

title: EOT apply shifts EVERY task (incl. completed/past) by approved days, with no idempotency guard
evidence: The /eot/:eotId/apply handler loads ALL non-deleted tasks for the project (`select('id,start_date,end_date')...eq('project_id',projectId)`) and unconditionally adds days_approved to every start/end: `start_date: task.start_date ? addDays(task.start_date, days) : null`. There is no filter on status (completed tasks shifted), no filter on tasks before the EOT/delay event, and no guard on eot.applied_at — the only state check is `eot.status !== 'approved'` (line 1373), which still passes on a second apply because status stays 'approved' after applying.
repro: Approve an EOT for days_approved=10 and POST .../apply twice. First call shifts all tasks +10 days (including 'Slab pour' completed last month, now dated in the future). Second call shifts everything another +10 (=20 total) — applied_at is set but never re-checked, so re-apply is not blocked.
impact: An EOT extends a contractual completion deadline / specific downstream works — it must not relocate work already done or duplicate-shift. Completed-task dates become wrong (corrupts as-built record and any baseline drift / slip-insight comparison that reads start/end). Double-apply silently doubles the contractual extension. EOT days are contractually and financially significant.
fixSketch: Guard idempotency: `if (eot.applied_at) return err(...,'EOT already applied')`. Only shift tasks at/after the EOT's effective date and exclude status in ('complete','cancelled'); ideally shift only the affected task subtree, not the whole project. Wrap the per-row updates so a partial failure doesn't leave a half-shifted schedule.

title: Schedule PATCH (and EOT/baseline/ripple handlers) leak raw Postgres error strings to the browser and bypass ok()/err()
evidence: `catch (e) { ... return res.status(502).json({ ok: false, error: e?.message || String(e) }); }` — e is the raw Supabase/Postgres error. The CHECK on task_type (mig 072) and the unvalidated write `if (body.task_type != null) patch.task_type = String(body.task_type);` (line 1037) means a body with e.g. task_type:'foo' makes the update throw `new row for relation "schedule_tasks" violates check constraint "schedule_tasks_task_type_check"`, which is returned verbatim. This violates the project law: 'Never expose raw Supabase/Postgres error strings — use translateDbError' and 'always use ok()/err() from apiResponse.mjs'.
repro: PATCH /api/schedule/task/:id with body { task_type: 'foo' } → 502 body { ok:false, error:'new row for relation "schedule_tasks" violates check constraint "schedule_tasks_task_type_check"' }. Same for any constraint/type violation across these handlers.
impact: Internal schema (table/constraint/column names) leaks to any authenticated user; users see DB jargon instead of plain English. Inconsistent with the rest of the codebase's apiResponse contract. Lower severity than the logic bugs but a clear, repeatable law violation.
fixSketch: Route these handlers through err(res, status, translateDbError(e)) / ok(res, ...) from apiResponse.mjs, and whitelist body.task_type against the constants enum before writing so the CHECK is never hit by user input.

title: Idempotency guard ignores trade — a sub covering 2 trades only gets the FIRST RFQ; the rest are silently skipped
evidence: const { data: prior } = await sb.from("rfqs").select("id").eq("job_id", jobIdM).eq("subcontractor_id", subIdM).eq("status", "sent").limit(1); if (prior && prior.length) { results.push({ ok: true, to, skipped: true }); continue; }  — the guard keys ONLY on (job_id, subcontractor_id, status='sent') with NO trade filter. rfqs has no unique constraint preventing multiple trades per (job,sub) (migrations 001/009 — no UNIQUE on job_id+subcontractor_id).
repro: In RfqEngine select one subcontractor as a recipient for two trades they service (e.g. a sub registered for both plumbing and gas, or any sub picked under two selected trades). handleSend() sends rows sequentially via sendOneRow(). Row 1 (trade A) sends and sets rfqs.status='sent'. Row 2 (trade B, SAME subcontractor_id + jobId) hits /api/rfq/send: the guard finds the trade-A 'sent' row and returns {ok:true,skipped:true}. sendOneRow treats skipped as success, deletes its queued rfq (line 2142), marks the row 'sent' and shows 'Already sent to <sub>'. The trade-B RFQ email is NEVER sent and no rfqs row survives for trade B.
impact: Subcontractors who quote multiple trades silently never receive the RFQ for their second/third trade on a job. The trade looks 'sent' in the UI and the row's queued rfq is deleted, so there is no record the email was skipped beyond a transient banner. A whole trade package can go un-tendered with the team believing it went out.
fixSketch: Add .eq("trade", <this message's trade label/id>) to the idempotency SELECT (or key the guard on rfqId / a (job_id,subcontractor_id,trade) tuple) so the dedupe is per-trade, not per-subcontractor. The client already inserts a queued rfq with the trade label — guard against a prior SENT row for the SAME trade only.

title: Role-bypass: /api/po/issue and the entire /api/rfq + /api/rfq-packages surface are requireAuth-only (no requireRole) despite the code comment claiming admin+supervisor
evidence: Comment at 829: "NOT gated here on purpose: /api/po (PO issuance is done from the ops Procurement view — admin+supervisor)" — but the admin prefix loop (846) lists only /api/finance,/api/sales,/api/marketing,/api/intelligence,/api/cost-intelligence,/api/cost-model,/api/fee-proposal,/api/tender,/api/templates, and the only added role gate is app.use("/api/carpentry", requireAuth, requireRole("admin","supervisor")) at 851. All PO/RFQ handlers (po/issue at module4Routes.mjs:570, rfq/send at dev-api.mjs:1873, every rfq-packages route in rfqPackageRoutes.mjs) carry only requireAuth, and requireRole appears nowhere inside those handlers (grep returned no matches).
repro: Authenticate as a non-admin, non-supervisor employee (requireAuth.mjs only rejects role==='client', line 24). POST /api/po/issue with a valid body → a PO PDF is generated, emailed to the vendor, inserted into purchase_orders, and synced to Buildexact. Likewise POST /api/rfq/send emails subbies, and GET /api/rfq-packages / GET /api/rfq-packages/:id returns every package including rfq_recipients.quote_amount (vendor cost $).

The intended gate documented in the comment was never wired, so the protection is illusory.

Verify the ops Procurement UI role matches whatever gate is chosen.

title: RFQ package silently lost if /api/rfq-packages create returns a non-OK JSON error after all RFQs were emailed
evidence: const pkgRes = await authFetch("/api/rfq-packages", {...}); const pkgJson = await pkgRes.json().catch(() => null); resetRfqSession(); if (pkgJson?.packageId) { navigate(...); return; } ... setBanner({ variant: "success", title: "RFQs dispatched", body: "All RFQs sent and logged — starting a fresh RFQ session." }); — the success path checks only res.json() truthiness, never pkgRes.ok. resetRfqSession() runs unconditionally before the packageId check.
repro: Send all RFQs (they go out and are logged). The package POST then 500s server-side — e.g. rfqPackageRoutes.mjs:427 buildRfqTradeIntelligence (which makes DB calls that can throw) rejects, or any tsErr/pkgErr in the insert loop (rfqPackageRoutes.mjs:453/477) → err(res,500,...). pkgRes.ok is false, pkgJson is {ok:false,error:...} with no packageId. Client does NOT throw (it only catches network errors), so resetRfqSession() wipes the whole session, no navigation occurs, and the green 'RFQs dispatched' banner is shown.
impact: The emails were sent but the persistent RFQ package (trade scopes + recipients that drive the Tender Board / quote tracker / follow-ups / coverage) is never created, and the in-browser session that could rebuild it is destroyed. The user sees a success message and has no way to recover the package short of re-keying every trade scope. Quote tracking for that whole tender is silently broken.
fixSketch: Gate on pkgRes.ok && pkgJson?.packageId before resetRfqSession(); on failure, do NOT reset — surface an error banner ('RFQs were sent but the package could not be saved — retry') and keep the session so finalizeAllSentPackage can be re-invoked, or retry the POST.

title: Issue-PO never stamps ordered_at → supplier lead-time learning loop silently never fires
repro: 1) Draft a PO on a builder_supplied item (status→po_drafted). 2) Click 'Issue' (POST /api/procurement/items/:id/issue-po) → status=po_sent, ordered_at stays NULL. 3) Later set status='delivered' via the dropdown → PATCH fires onItemDelivered → captureLeadObservation reads ordered_at=null → returns null at line 32 → no supplier_lead_observations row → refreshSupplierPerformance is skipped (onItemDelivered line 97 guards on `obs`). Supplier performance silently stays empty/stale forever; backup-supplier ranking and learned lead times degrade to defaults. fixSketch: In issue-po, stamp ordered_at on the item update when it is null, e.g. include `ordered_at: item.ordered_at || new Date().toISOString()` in the procurement_items.update at line 464. (Cleaner: route the issue-po item write through applyLifecycle so po_sent stamping is centralized.)

title: PO drafted/issued off cost_allowance alone contributes $0 to committed cost (Finance under-reports)
repro: 1) Item has cost_allowance=$50,000 but no approved_amount/quoted_amount (admin never typed an Approved figure). 2) Draft PO → po total_amount=50000 (passes amount>0). 3) Issue PO → real PDF emailed to supplier quoting $50k inc GST, item→po_sent. 4) GET /api/procurement/jobs/:id/committed-cost (and financeCCRoutes.mjs:718 committed_cost) returns 0 for that line. title: draft-po has no existing-PO guard → re-drafting orphans the prior purchase_orders row
repro: Draft a PO (item.purchase_order_id = PO_A, status=po_drafted). Then call POST /api/procurement/items/:id/draft-po again (e.g. after editing approved_amount, or because the item status was manually set above po_drafted so the frontend 'PO' button never flips to 'Issue' — line 389 keeps status unchanged when rank>=po_drafted, and Procurement.jsx:414 still renders the PO button for any status that isn't exactly po_drafted/po_sent). title: Buildexact API estimate path drops the builder's margin → fee proposal underpriced (markup=0, cost×1.1)
file: server/lib/buildexactParser.mjs:730-813 (entered via costIntelligenceEstimate.mjs:225 pullBuildexactEstimate → buildexactDeepIntegration.mjs:66 normaliseBuildexactEstimatePayload)
evidence: itemAmount() reads only cost-ish keys: `Number(pick(item, ["total","Total","amount","Amount","lineTotal","LineTotal","subtotal","Subtotal"], 0))` (line 731). The category roll-up then does `cat.subtotal_ex_gst += total; cat.subtotal_inc_gst += Math.round(total * 1.1 * 100) / 100;` (lines 772-773) and the estimate returns `markup_amount: 0, markup_percent: 0` with `net_total = sum(subtotal_ex_gst)` and `estimate_total ... || categories.reduce((s,c)=>s+subtotal_inc_gst)` (lines 797, 806-810). No markup / TotalIncMarkupAndTax / sell-price field is ever read (grep for markup|sellPrice across buildexactClient.mjs + buildexactDeepIntegration.mjs returns nothing). Contrast the XLSX estimateitems path, which deliberately separates cost vs sell: `subtotal_sell_ex_gst = cost + markup` (buildexactParser.mjs:486) and derives markup_amount/markup_percent (lines 511-512).
repro: In FeeProposalWizard, link a job with buildexact_job_id and click 'Pull from Buildexact' (pullFromBuildexact, FeeProposalWizard.jsx:439). mergeParsedToProposal sets total_inc_gst = parsed.estimate_total (feeProposalDefaults.js:125). For an estimate whose line 'Total' = cost ex-markup (e.g. $500k cost at 20% margin), the headline becomes $500k×1.1 = $550k instead of the correct $600k×1.1 = $660k — a $110k under-quote sent to the client. The same parsed.categories also seed job_budgets/normalized_costs via parseEstimateIntoCostCategories (costIntelligenceEstimate.mjs:118-167) at cost, not sell, skewing Cost Intelligence benchmarks too.
impact: Client-facing fee proposal can be quoted at cost+GST with the builder's margin silently omitted whenever the proposal is built via the Buildexact API pull (rather than the XLSX estimateitems export). Direct lost income / mispriced contract. Also pollutes cost benchmarks.
fixSketch: Mirror the estimateitems logic in normaliseBuildexactEstimatePayload: read the per-line markup + inc-markup-and-tax fields from the Buildxact DTO (the v3 estimate item DTO exposes them), compute subtotal_sell_ex_gst = cost + markup, set total_inc_gst from the sell-inc figure, and populate markup_amount/markup_percent. Replace the hardcoded *1.1 with incGst()/GST_RATE. If the API genuinely cannot return sell prices, the pull must refuse to populate total_inc_gst rather than silently emit cost+GST.

title: Hardcoded *1.1 GST in fee-proposal summary builder (law violation + understates price in fallback)
evidence: `const inc = Number(c.subtotal_inc_gst ?? Math.round(ex * 1.1 * 100) / 100);` where `const ex = Number(c.subtotal_ex_gst ?? c.subtotal ?? 0);`. CLAUDE.md Standards: 'Never hardcode 0.1 or * 1.1 — use GST_RATE, incGst(), gstAmount()'. The same pattern is mirrored client-side in feeProposalDefaults.js:71 and FeeProposalWizard.jsx:375. Worse than a style nit: subtotal_ex_gst on the estimateitems path is COST ex-markup (buildexactParser.mjs:490), so when subtotal_inc_gst is missing the fallback renders cost×1.1 in the client summary, omitting markup.
repro: Build a proposal with a category object that lacks subtotal_inc_gst (e.g. a hand-added category in the wizard, or a persisted category reloaded via dbToProposal where the stored category JSON had no inc field). buildSummaryRowsFromParse / the wizard summaryRows show cost×1.1 for that category in the client-facing 'Total (inc GST)' column.
impact: Client summary line can understate a category by the markup amount; violates the money law and will be flagged by /check. Low blast radius because all three parser paths normally set subtotal_inc_gst, but real for manual/edge categories.
fixSketch: Import GST_RATE/incGst from constants (or the server constant pattern used in module4Routes.mjs:34) and replace `ex * 1.1` with `incGst(ex)`. But the deeper fix is to never fall back to ex×rate for client price — fall back to the sell figure, not cost.

title: Cost Intelligence routes leak raw Postgres/error strings to the client
file: server/lib/costIntelligenceRoutes.mjs:56,81,93,340,457,477,541,588,632,701 (and ok:true responses are not via apiResponse.mjs)
evidence: Every catch block does `res.status(500).json({ ok: false, error: e.message })` (e.g. line 56 `res.status(500).json({ ok: false, error: e.message });`, line 340, line 701). CLAUDE.md: 'Never expose raw Supabase/Postgres error strings — use translateDbError(error)'. The module also never imports ok/err/rowToCamel from apiResponse.mjs, so successful rows are returned raw snake_case (e.g. metrics, normalized_costs with amount_ex_gst), which CostIntelligence.jsx then reads as snake_case (CostIntelligence.jsx:1257-1262 `c.amount_ex_gst`).
repro: Trigger any DB error on an admin-token request to e.g. POST /api/cost-intelligence/jobs/:jobId/sync-estimate; the raw thrown message (potentially a Postgres constraint/string) is returned verbatim in the JSON error field.

fixSketch: Route all responses through ok()/err()/translateDbError from apiResponse.mjs and rowToCamel the returned rows; update CostIntelligence.jsx to read camelCase. At minimum wrap thrown messages with translateDbError before returning.

title: Headline TOTAL_INC_GST is a free-text override with no reconciliation against the category summary
evidence: The wizard exposes an editable numeric field that sets proposal.total_inc_gst directly (`onChange={(e) => setProposal((p) => ({ ...p, total_inc_gst: Number(e.target.value) || 0 }))}`, line 1085). proposalToDocxData renders the headline from this field independently of the SUMMARY_ROWS table: `TOTAL_INC_GST: formatCurrencyAud(p.total_inc_gst || 0)` (line 296) and `TOTAL_COST_GST` (line 301), while SUMMARY_ROWS comes from buildSummaryRowsFromParse over categories (line 300/276-278). There is no check that the sum of summary rows equals total_inc_gst.
repro: Import an estimate (summary rows sum to $X), then edit the 'Total inc GST (editable)' field to $Y ≠ $X, generate the DOCX. The proposal shows a category breakdown summing to $X but a headline grand total of $Y, with no warning. Also occurs naturally because the $0-category drop (transform line 173) and per-row rounding can make the visible rows not reconcile to estimate_total.
