fixSketch: Compute the headline as the sum of the (non-dropped) category summary rows by default and only allow an explicit override with a visible 'overridden — does not match breakdown' warning; or validate |sum(rows) − total_inc_gst| ≤ rounding tolerance before generate/send and block/confirm on mismatch.

title: convert-to-job address-dedup overwrites another party's canonical client facts (cross-lead contamination)
evidence: Dedup matches ANY existing job by address: `if (addr.normalised) { const { data } = await sb.from("jobs").select("*").eq("address_normalised", addr.normalised).limit(1); job = data?.[0] || null; }` … `if (!job) { ... ilike("address", rawAddress) ... }`. If a job is found, step 4's insert is skipped, then step 5 unconditionally stamps the NEW lead's identity onto it: `const carry = [["address",rawAddress],["client_name",clientName||null],["client_email",lead.email...],["client_phone",lead.phone...],...]; for (...) await setFact(job.id, key, value, {source:"system", reason:"lead_conversion", actorId});`. There is NO check that the matched job is unlinked / belongs to this lead. In jobFactRegistry.mjs client_name (line 35) and client_email (line 41) are `tier:"consequential"` facts stored on jobs and consumed by finance/portal/claims/variations.
repro: 1) A job already exists for '12 Smith St' (created via POST /api/jobs for client A, or a prior lead). 2) A different lead for client B also has site_address '12 Smith St' (subdivision / duplicate address / re-enquiry). 3) Click 'Create job from lead' on lead B → POST /api/sales/leads/:id/convert-to-job. 4) convertLeadToJob dedups onto client A's job, stamps client_name=B, client_email=B over A's values, and sets leads(B).job_id = A's job. Finance/portal now show B on A's project; lead B is welded to A's job.
impact: Canonical Data Law violation: a consequential-tier identity fact (client_name/email) on an existing job is silently overwritten by an unrelated lead, and the lead is mis-linked to a foreign job. Downstream finance invoices, portal access and progress-claim/variation emails address the wrong client. Also the matched job's jobs.lead_id is never back-filled, so the reverse spine link stays stale/null.
fixSketch: Before adopting a deduped job, guard identity: only reuse the existing job if it is unlinked (job.lead_id == null || job.lead_id == lead.id) AND its client identity is empty or matches; otherwise refuse with a 409 ('A job already exists at this address for a different client'). When a fresh job is created the insert sets lead_id; when an existing unlinked job is adopted, also `update({lead_id: lead.id})`. Never overwrite a non-empty consequential fact via the system-sourced conversion carry.

title: leads.stage has no DB CHECK constraint and all code hardcodes stage strings instead of LEAD_STAGES — silent pipeline drift
evidence: Schema: `stage text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'enquiry',` with no CHECK (grep for a stage CHECK across all migrations finds only leads_ptsa_status_check in 045 — none for stage). The PATCH handler accepts the client value verbatim: salesRoutes.mjs:556 `if (updates.stage && current?.stage && updates.stage !== current.stage) { ... }` then `sb.from("leads").update(updates)` — no whitelist. constants.js exports LEAD_STAGES but salesRoutes.mjs imports none of it; SalesPipeline.jsx (STAGES array, lines 7-16) and LeadDetail.jsx (STAGES, STAGE_ORDER, GATE_REQUIREMENTS, lines 8-77) all hardcode literals. moveStage()/advanceStage() send whatever string they hold.

The row is updated to that arbitrary value, a stage_change activity is logged, and the lead silently vanishes from the kanban (no STAGES entry matches) and is excluded from scorecard STAGE_PROB buckets (defaults to prob 0). No error surfaces.

The DB cannot catch it because there is no CHECK; constants.js exists precisely to prevent this but is unused on this spine.
fixSketch: Add a migration `ALTER TABLE leads ADD CONSTRAINT leads_stage_check CHECK (stage IN ('enquiry','qualify','discovery','winning_offer','fee_proposal','accepted','tender','won','nurture','lost'))`, and have salesRoutes.mjs import LEAD_STAGES and validate `Object.values(LEAD_STAGES).includes(updates.stage)` (err 400 via translateDbError otherwise). Replace hardcoded STAGES literals in both pages with constants.js.

title: Bulk email send + contact PII are reachable by any non-admin staff token (no requireRole on /api/crm)
evidence: The prefix-gate loop omits /api/crm on purpose: dev-api.mjs:830-831 comment — "/api/crm (... its sensitive endpoints already carry requireRole(\"admin\"))". But the bulk-send endpoint is requireAuth only: crmRoutes.mjs:1042 `app.post("/api/crm/sends/:sid/send", requireAuth, async (req, res) => {` — no requireRole. Same for `POST /api/crm/sends` (1042… 991), `GET /api/crm/contacts` (359, returns email/phone for every contact), `GET /api/crm/lists/:id` (835, returns member emails), `POST /api/crm/lists/:id/import` (919). Only the job-roles/fee endpoints (620-742) carry requireRole("admin"). requireAuth (requireAuth.mjs:31-37 is a SEPARATE export and is NOT applied) blocks only role==='client' (requireAuth.mjs:24).
repro: Log in as a supervisor or employee (non-admin staff) to obtain a valid Supabase token. The frontend hides Marketing (App.jsx:271 allowed=['admin']) so the UI is invisible, but the API is open: `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <supervisor_token>' https://hub/api/crm/contacts` returns the full contact list with names, emails, phones; `curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer <supervisor_token>' https://hub/api/crm/sends/<draftId>/send` fires a real bulk Resend campaign. Both return 200, not 403.
impact: Privilege escalation + PII exposure: any of the company's supervisors/employees (not just directors) can exfiltrate the entire marketing/CRM contact database (names, emails, phones — Spam Act / Privacy Act PII) and can trigger company-wide bulk email campaigns under the Blue Leaf sending domain without authorisation. The comment claiming sensitive CRM endpoints "already carry requireRole(admin)" is false for the send + contact-read + import endpoints.
fixSketch: Either add "/api/crm" to the prefix-gate loop with a route-level carve-out for the public GET /api/crm/unsubscribe (already registered without auth) and the webhook, OR add `requireRole("admin")` to every write/PII endpoint: POST /api/crm/sends, POST /api/crm/sends/:sid/send, GET /api/crm/contacts, GET /api/crm/contacts/:id, GET/POST /api/crm/lists*, POST .../import. Confirm the intended CRM operator role first (admin-only per App.jsx).

title: Smart-list sends ignore unsubscribe/consent entirely — unsubscribed contacts get re-emailed
evidence: Smart-list recipient resolution: `if (list.list_type === "smart") { const memberIds = await smartListMembers(...); ... sb().from("crm_contacts").select(...).in("id", memberIds.map(r=>r.id)).not("email","is",null); recipients = contacts || []; }`. smartListMembers (147-165) filters only on is_archived/status/contact_type/created_this_month — it never consults mailing_list_members.unsubscribed_at or email_unsubscribes. The manual-list branch correctly filters `.is("unsubscribed_at", null)` (1075) but smart lists have NO member rows, so no unsubscribe state exists to filter on. Public unsubscribe (1213-1216) and webhook complaint/bounce handlers (1285-1297) only touch mailing_list_members rows, which smart lists don't have.
repro: 1) A contact with status='past_client' clicks Unsubscribe in a campaign, or marks it as spam (email.complained webhook). 2) A smart list with smart_filter {status:['past_client']} exists. 3) Admin sends to that smart list via POST /api/crm/sends/:sid/send. The unsubscribed/complained contact still matches the filter (contact.status unchanged) and is re-added to `recipients` and emailed again.
impact: Australian Spam Act 2003 breach: emailing a contact after they unsubscribed or lodged a spam complaint. For smart lists there is no suppression mechanism at all — the 'unsubscribe' the footer promises is silently ineffective for any contact reachable via a smart list. Compounds spam complaints and risks domain reputation / legal exposure.
fixSketch: Before building `recipients` (both branches), load the global suppression set: SELECT contact_id FROM email_unsubscribes (and/or any mailing_list_members where unsubscribed_at IS NOT NULL) and exclude those contact_ids. Better: enforce a global per-contact suppression (e.g. a do_not_email flag on crm_contacts set by any unsubscribe/complaint/bounce) and filter every send path against it.

title: Link-unsubscribe is per-list only; no global suppression — contact still emailed via other lists
evidence: Public unsubscribe handler: `const { contactId, listId, sendId } = payload; await ...from("mailing_list_members").update({unsubscribed_at..., unsubscribed_via:"link"}).eq("contact_id", contactId).eq("list_id", listId);` — scoped to the single list_id baked into the JWT (token minted per-list at 1104 `jwt.sign({ contactId, listId, sendId }, ...)`). Contrast the bounce/complaint webhook handlers (1285-1288, 1295-1297) which deliberately update across ALL lists (no .eq("list_id")). The unsubscribe page text (1234) tells the user they "won't receive further emails from this list" but the brand/sender is the same across every list.
repro: A contact is on 'Newsletter' (manual) and also matches 'Past Clients' (smart). They click Unsubscribe from a Newsletter email → only their Newsletter membership row is flagged. The next Past-Clients smart send still emails them (see also smart-list finding). Even across two manual lists, unsubscribing from one leaves the other active.
impact: A recipient who reasonably believes they have opted out of Blue Leaf marketing keeps receiving it via other lists, a Spam Act consent-withdrawal failure. The webhook path treats complaints globally, so behaviour is inconsistent: a spam-complaint suppresses everywhere, a polite unsubscribe-link click does not.
fixSketch: Treat unsubscribe as a global consent withdrawal: on link-unsubscribe, also update all mailing_list_members for that contact_id (mirror the bounce/complaint handlers) and/or set a contact-level suppression flag that all send paths honour. Keep the per-list row update for audit granularity but add the global suppression.

title: increment_send_stat double-counts on Resend webhook retries (no event-id idempotency)
evidence: Each webhook branch unconditionally bumps the counter: `await getServiceSupabase().rpc("increment_send_stat", { p_resend_email_id: emailId, p_field: "delivered_count" })`. The RPC (073) does `UPDATE email_sends SET delivered_count = COALESCE(delivered_count,0)+1`. The recipient-status UPDATEs above each RPC are idempotent (set to a fixed value), but the counter is a blind +1 with no guard on whether this event was already processed. Resend (Svix) retries the SAME event on any non-2xx or timeout, and there is no resend_event_id dedup table for delivered/opened/clicked (only complaint/unsubscribe rows carry resend_event_id, and even those have no UNIQUE constraint — mig 061:152-160).
repro: Resend delivers `email.delivered` for emailId X. The handler runs (counter→1) but the response is delayed/errs or Resend retries per its at-least-once policy. The duplicate event runs again → delivered_count→2 for one recipient. opened_count is even worse: a recipient opening an email 5 times fires 5 `email.opened` events, each +1, so opened_count can exceed total_recipients; the UI open-rate math (MailingLists.jsx:454 `Math.round(openedCount/deliveredCount*100)`) then shows >100%.
impact: Campaign analytics (delivered/opened/clicked/bounced/unsubscribed counts) are inflated and unreliable — open rates can exceed 100%. Not money, but the stats drive marketing decisions and the dashboard is visibly wrong.
fixSketch: Make stats idempotent: count distinct recipient state transitions instead of incrementing on every event. Either (a) only increment when the recipient row actually transitions into the state (e.g. UPDATE ... WHERE status<>'delivered' RETURNING, and increment only if a row changed), or (b) derive counts on read via COUNT over email_send_recipients by status rather than storing running totals. For opens specifically, gate on opened_at IS NULL before counting a first open.

title: All CRM created_by / added_by audit fields silently stored NULL (req.user never set)
evidence: requireAuth sets the caller as req.caller: `req.caller = { ...profile, email: user.email };` (requireAuth.mjs:27) — it never sets req.user. grep confirms `req.user =` appears nowhere in server/. Yet CRM inserts read the wrong property: contact create `created_by: req.user?.id || null` (419), interaction `created_by: req.user?.id` (533), list create (826), list member add `added_by: req.user?.id` (878), CSV import created_by/added_by (947,963), send draft created_by (1004). All evaluate to undefined → stored null. The job-roles endpoints correctly use req.caller?.id (683), proving the intended property.
repro: Add a contact to a mailing list via POST /api/crm/lists/:id/members, then SELECT added_by FROM mailing_list_members WHERE ... → it is NULL even though an authenticated admin performed the action. Same for who created any contact, list, send, or import batch.
impact: The Spam Act audit trail the schema was built for (who added this contact with what consent, who created/sent this campaign) is blank for every CRM record. In a consent dispute the company cannot show which staff member added a contact or sent a campaign. Silent — no error, lint/build pass.
fixSketch: Replace `req.user?.id` with `req.caller?.id` in all CRM inserts (and audit other modules for the same typo). Consider a shared helper or grep gate in /check to ban req.user where requireAuth is the middleware.

title: Final Assembly + Re-export run ffmpeg on a Supabase storage path as if it were a local file (and never download it)
evidence: assembleExport: `await applyLUTs(originalPath, isDLogM, colour_preset, lutPath);` where applyLUTs runs `"${ffmpeg}" -i "${inputPath}" ...` (marketingMedia.mjs:274). The route passes `exportRec.marketing_media_assets.storage_path` (a Supabase object key like 'uploads/2025/06/<uuid>.mp4') directly as originalPath (marketingRoutes.mjs:1480). reexportAsset is identical: `await applyLUTs(originalPath, ...)` with originalPath = `asset.storage_path` (marketingRoutes.mjs:1067). Neither function calls sb.storage.download() — contrast runFullDronePipeline which explicitly downloads first: `.download(filePath)` then `await writeFile(localSrc, ...)` and comments 'all ffmpeg steps use this, never filePath directly' (marketingMedia.mjs:483-491).
repro: Upload any photo/video so it has a storage_path, then call POST /api/marketing/media/:id/export {export_format:'1x1'} (or run Final Assembly via POST /api/marketing/assemble with a valid export_id + music_track_id). ffmpeg receives `-i uploads/2025/06/<uuid>.mp4` which does not exist on the API server's local FS → ffmpeg exits non-zero → catch sets the export row status='failed'. The export never produces output.
impact: Final Assembly (music + colour grade) and additional-aspect-ratio re-export silently fail for every asset. These are core Stage-2 deliverables; the marketing team can never produce a music-scored or re-cropped clip through these endpoints. The failure is only visible as a 'failed' export row.
fixSketch: In assembleExport and reexportAsset, download the source from Supabase to a temp file first (mirror runFullDronePipeline lines 483-491: const {data}=await sb.storage.from('marketing-media').download(originalPath); await writeFile(localSrc, Buffer.from(await data.arrayBuffer()))), then pass localSrc to applyLUTs. Guard against a null storage_path (see related finding).

title: Streamed videos (/upload-video) are never persisted to storage — storage_path stays null and the temp source is deleted, so export/assembly is impossible
evidence: The insert sets `storage_path: null` (line 894) with the comment 'raw video stays on server temp disk'. Only the thumbnail is uploaded to Supabase (lines 919-921). The background pipeline is invoked with `cleanupLocalPath: true` (line 937), and runVideoIntelligencePipeline deletes the temp file in its finally block (`if (ownsTmp && tmpPath) await rm(tmpPath...)`, videoIntelligence.mjs:612-615). The raw video is therefore gone after the pipeline and was never stored anywhere durable.
repro: Upload a drone .mp4 via the Media tab (routes to POST /api/marketing/media/upload-video). After the background pipeline finishes, the asset row has storage_path = null and the temp file is removed. Now click 'Final Assembly' → POST /api/marketing/assemble selects storage_path (null) and calls assembleExport(null, ...) → ffmpeg `-i "null"` fails. Same for POST /api/marketing/media/:id/export.
impact: Every large/drone video (the exact use case this endpoint was built for — bypassing Supabase's 50MB limit) becomes un-exportable. The story-sequence preview works (it uses frames), but no final rendered video can ever be produced from a streamed upload. On Railway's ephemeral disk the source is unrecoverable.
fixSketch: Upload the raw video to Supabase storage (e.g. uploads/YYYY/MM/<assetId>.<ext>) before/after the pipeline and set storage_path on the asset row, OR keep the temp file and have assemble/export resolve the local path. At minimum, /assemble and /export must reject assets with null storage_path with a clear error rather than feeding null to ffmpeg.

title: Media consent (consent_for_marketing) is not enforced on AI content generation, streaming, preload preview, or video re-export — only on final /assemble
evidence: The only consent check in the module is at /assemble: `if (!exportRec.marketing_media_assets?.consent_for_marketing) return res.status(403)...` (marketingRoutes.mjs:1460-1462). /generate accepts photo_asset_id and downloads+feeds the image to Claude to produce a publishable caption (buildGenerationMessages, lines 97-128) with no consent lookup. /campaigns/:id/preload pulls analysed photos and generates ready-to-save captions for them (lines 731-812) with no consent check. /media/:id/export produces a new publishable rendered asset (lines 1047-1075) with no consent check. The column defaults to false (migration 046:108: `consent_for_marketing boolean DEFAULT false`), so freshly uploaded client photos are non-consented by default yet flow straight into generated marketing copy and exports.
repro: Upload a client site photo (consent_for_marketing=false by default). Call POST /api/marketing/generate with that photo_asset_id (or run a campaign preload) → returns finished Instagram/Facebook copy built from that non-consented image, which the user can then save+publish. Separately, POST /api/marketing/media/:id/export on a non-consented asset renders a new export. The UI badge says 'No consent' but the server never blocks these paths.
impact: Per CLAUDE.md consent is a compliance-tier fact: content derived from a client's project photos can be generated and exported for publication without the consent gate the product clearly intends. The single /assemble check is trivially bypassed via /export (which produces a renderable file) or by publishing AI copy generated from the image. Privacy/consent breach risk.
fixSketch: Add a consent_for_marketing lookup wherever a specific media asset drives publishable output: in buildGenerationMessages when photo_asset_id is supplied (skip image or 403), in /campaigns/:id/preload filter to `.eq('consent_for_marketing', true)`, and in /media/:id/export return 403 when the asset is non-consented — mirroring the /assemble guard.

title: Intelligence dashboard AI summary uses a stale/legacy model id and fails silently, so the summary never renders
evidence: `model: "claude-haiku-20240307"` — every other Haiku call in the codebase uses `claude-haiku-4-5` (e.g. marketingIntelligenceRoutes.mjs:1378 and :1525, videoIntelligence.mjs:25, procurementAiService.mjs:19). The call is wrapped in `try { ... } catch { /* non-fatal */ }` (lines 519-544) and only writes the cache on success (`if (aiSummary) _aiCache.set(weekKey, aiSummary)`), so a model-not-found error is swallowed and the cache key is never populated.
repro: Load GET /api/intelligence/dashboard with >=3 published content items and a valid ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. If the account/SDK no longer serves the legacy 'claude-haiku-20240307' id (it is a Claude 3 id, deprecated relative to the 4.x ids used everywhere else), callAI throws, the catch eats it, ai_summary stays null, and because nothing is cached the failing call is re-attempted on every dashboard load that week.
impact: The dashboard's AI performance summary silently never appears (looks like 'no data'), and each load re-incurs a failed (billable-attempt) Anthropic call instead of being cached. A reviewer running lint/build would never catch it because the error is caught.
fixSketch: Change the model id to the standard `claude-haiku-4-5` used by the sibling calls in the same file, and log the catch (console.warn) instead of swallowing silently so future model breakage is visible.

title: Meta access token sent in the URL query string for Graph API insight fetches
evidence: `const url = \`https://graph.facebook.com/v19.0/${pub.platform_post_id}/insights?metric=${metricsField}&access_token=${accessToken}\`; const resp = await fetch(url);` — the long-lived META_ACCESS_TOKEN is placed in the query string. Contrast the Google syncs in the same file which correctly use a header: `headers: { Authorization: \`Bearer ${accessToken}\` }` (e.g. lines 705, 738, 858).
repro: Trigger POST /api/intelligence/sync/meta (admin). The full request URL including access_token is what gets recorded by any intermediary/proxy logging, and on a non-2xx response the code path does not log the URL, but error tooling, APM, or fetch instrumentation that captures request URLs will capture the token.
impact: Tokens in URLs are higher-exposure than headers (logged by proxies, browser/network tooling, server access logs, error aggregators). A leaked META_ACCESS_TOKEN grants read access to the business's Instagram/Facebook insights and potentially more depending on scope. Lower severity because the call is server-to-server and admin-only, but it is an avoidable secret-in-URL.
fixSketch: Move the token to an Authorization header: `fetch(\`https://graph.facebook.com/v19.0/${id}/insights?metric=${metricsField}\`, { headers: { Authorization: \`Bearer ${accessToken}\` } })`, matching the Google sync pattern in the same file.

title: Schedule write routes are requireAuth-only — an 'employee' (UI: schedule view-only) can create/edit/delete any project's schedule tasks
evidence: scheduleRoutes: `app.post("/api/schedule/:projectId/task", requireAuth, ...)`, `app.patch("/api/schedule/task/:id", requireAuth, ...)`, `app.delete("/api/schedule/task/:id", requireAuth, ...)` — none has requireRole. The dev-api.mjs prefix gate loop only iterates ["/api/finance","/api/sales","/api/marketing","/api/intelligence","/api/cost-intelligence","/api/cost-model","/api/fee-proposal","/api/tender","/api/templates"] (line 835-846) plus a single `app.use("/api/carpentry", requireAuth, requireRole("admin","supervisor"))` (851). /api/schedule and /api/operations appear in NEITHER. requireAuth (requireAuth.mjs:6-29) sets req.caller and blocks only role==='client'; it does NOT check admin/supervisor/employee.
repro: Log in as an 'employee' role user (roles.js: ROLE_EMPLOYEE = 'site-only', `editSchedule: (r) => ["admin","supervisor"].includes(r)` so employees are denied edit in the UI, and ROLE_DESCRIPTIONS.employee = 'schedule view only'). Grab the Supabase access token from the browser session, then: `curl -X DELETE https://API/api/schedule/task/<any-task-id> -H "Authorization: Bearer <employee-token>"` → returns {ok:true,deleted:...} and soft-deletes the task. Same for POST /api/schedule/:projectId/task and PATCH /api/schedule/task/:id (date shifts, percent_complete, etc.).
impact: Server-side role bypass. A site-only employee (the lowest-trust staff role) can mutate or destroy the construction programme for ANY project — delete tasks, shift dates, mark complete — none of which the UI exposes to them. The frontend role checks (can.editSchedule) are the ONLY barrier, defeated by a direct API call. This is the same class as the 'frontend hides it but the API doesn't gate it' bugs the prefix loop was added to fix (see dev-api.mjs:825-851 comment), but operations/schedule were left out of that loop.
fixSketch: Either add `app.use("/api/schedule", requireAuth, requireRole("admin","supervisor"))` and gate the write verbs, OR add inline requireRole("admin","supervisor") to the POST/PATCH/DELETE schedule routes (keeping GET routes at requireAuth so employees retain read/view). Mirror the carpentry pattern at dev-api.mjs:851. Note GETs (/api/schedule/:projectId, dashboard) should stay readable by employee per roles.js.

title: Public unauthenticated induction submit has 100MB body limit and no rate limiting — DoS / storage-exhaustion / data-injection
evidence: `app.post("/api/induction/:projectId/submit", async (req, res) => {...})` — no requireAuth, by design (public QR induction form, registered at dev-api.mjs:858, /api/induction is not in any gated prefix). The handler base64-decodes req.body.signatureImageBase64/signatureDataUrl, calls `buildInductionPdfBuffer(...)` (PDFKit render) and `fileJobRecord(...)` (Dropbox upload) and inserts a `site_inductions` row — all on the public path. The global body limit is `const JSON_BODY_LIMIT = process.env.BLUEPRINT_BODY_LIMIT || "100mb"; app.use(express.json({ limit: JSON_BODY_LIMIT, ... }))` (dev-api.mjs:808-815). grep for rateLimit/express-rate/429 across server/ shows ONLY Anthropic 429-retry logic — there is no request throttling middleware anywhere.
repro: Discover any valid projectId (induction QR URLs are /induct/:projectId and the GET /api/induction/:projectId/info is also public, so a project address page leaks it). Then in a loop: `curl -X POST https://API/api/induction/<projectId>/submit -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"personName":"x","company":"x","trade":"x","mobile":"x","emergencyContactName":"x","emergencyContactPhone":"x","siteRulesAcknowledged":true,"swmsAcknowledged":true,"signatureImageBase64":"<~70MB of base64>"}'`. Each request forces a PDFKit render of a multi-MB signature image + a Dropbox upload + a DB insert; fired concurrently it pegs CPU/memory and fills both Supabase rows and the Dropbox job-records folder. No auth, no captcha, no throttle stops it.
impact: Unauthenticated attacker can (a) exhaust the API server (PDFKit decoding 100MB images is CPU/RAM heavy → OOM/crash, taking the whole Express process down since the same process serves all staff/portal traffic), (b) flood Dropbox + site_inductions with junk inductions, (c) inject arbitrary attacker-controlled person_name/company/signature into a compliance record (the induction PDF is a WHS legal artefact). The 100mb limit (intended for Blueprint transcripts) silently applies to this public endpoint.
fixSketch: Mount a tighter express.json({limit:'2mb'}) specifically on /api/induction (signatures are small canvas PNGs), add an IP-based rate limiter (e.g. express-rate-limit) on the public /api/induction/* and other public surfaces, and cap/validate the decoded signature byte length before calling buildInductionPdfBuffer. Optionally require a short-lived signed project token in the QR URL rather than a raw projectId so the endpoint isn't enumerable.

title: Operations trade/PO routes leak subcontractor PII to lowest-trust 'employee' role (no role gate)
evidence: `app.get("/api/projects/:id/trades", requireAuth, ...)` selects `subcontractors ( id, business_name, contact, mobile, email )` and PO commercial status (po_number, ghosting flags) for ANY project id. `app.get("/api/projects/:id/supervisor-tasks", requireAuth, ...)` and `app.post("/api/trade-communication/respond", requireAuth, ...)` are also requireAuth-only. roles.js scopes supervisor-only/admin-only views: ROLE_DESCRIPTIONS.employee = 'Site access — site diary, WHS, schedule view only' and there is no can.* helper granting employees the Procurement/trades view. The dev-api prefix loop does not cover /api/projects.
repro: As an 'employee' token: `curl https://API/api/projects/<any-project-id>/trades -H 'Authorization: Bearer <employee-token>'` → returns full subcontractor contact list (emails, mobiles), PO numbers and 'is_ghosting' commercial intelligence for that job, plus POST /api/trade-communication/respond lets that same employee record a 'ghosted'/'unavailable' response which triggers a real outbound email to the subcontractor (operationsRoutes.mjs:371-384 sendPlainMail).
impact: An employee bypasses the UI's role scoping to harvest subcontractor PII and procurement status across every project, and can trigger automated subcontractor emails / create supervisor_tasks. No dollar amounts are in the select so it is not a $-to-cost-stripped-role breach, but it is a clear horizontal-privilege / PII-exposure gap (medium, not high, because all four staff roles are internal and trusted to a degree, and no cost figures leak).
fixSketch: Gate the /api/projects/:id/trades, /supervisor-tasks and /api/trade-communication/* routes (and /api/operations/*) with requireRole("admin","supervisor") — the Procurement/Trade Commitment view is a supervisor+admin feature per roles.js, not an employee one. Add /api/operations and /api/projects(-scoped trade routes) to the dev-api prefix loop or inline the role middleware.

title: syncProjectSwms deletes all SWMS links before re-inserting (non-atomic) — a failed insert leaves the public induction with zero SWMS to acknowledge
evidence:
await sb.from("project_swms").delete().eq("project_id", projectId);
      if (linkRows.length) await sb.from("project_swms").insert(linkRows);  — and the whole function is wrapped in try/catch that only console.warns: catch (e) { console.warn("[whs/project_swms-sync]", e?.message); }. project_swms is the exact table the PUBLIC induction reads to list SWMS for a worker to acknowledge (inductionRoutes.mjs:37-54 GET /info and :101-113 submit).
repro: 1. A project has its WHS profile saved once → project_swms populated with the derived SWMS. 2. Supervisor edits the questionnaire and hits Save again → PUT /api/whs/projects/:id/profile → syncProjectSwms runs. 3. The DELETE succeeds; the subsequent INSERT fails (transient DB/PostgREST error, or one swms_templates auto-create errors mid-loop) — the error is swallowed by the catch. 4. project_swms is now empty for that project. 5. A worker scans the induction QR → GET /api/induction/:projectId/info returns swms:[]; the worker is inducted (submit) with an empty swmsLines and no SWMS acknowledgement — a WHS compliance hole, and the prior links are gone with no recovery.

fixSketch: Compute linkRows first; only delete+insert when linkRows is non-empty, and do it atomically — either an upsert/diff (delete only the rows not in the new set, insert the new ones) or a Postgres RPC that wraps both in a transaction. title: Uploaded compliance documents with no expiry date always render as 'missing' (red/Action Required)
evidence: const computed = (docs || []).map((d) => ({ ...d, computed_status: d.expiry_date ? complianceStatusFromExpiry(d.expiry_date) : "missing" })); — and on insert (line 123) status = expiryDate ? complianceStatusFromExpiry(expiryDate) : "missing". The UI then renders red: WhsManager.jsx:310 `bad = docs.some((d) => ["expired","expiring_soon","missing"].includes(...))` and docChip() shows 'missing' as a dashed red chip.
repro: Add a compliance document (e.g. a trade Licence or SWMS) and leave Expiry date blank (the form allows it — WhsManager.jsx:161 sends expiryDate || null and the server only requires subcontractorId/documentType/fileBase64). The document is successfully uploaded to Dropbox and inserted, but its computed_status is 'missing', so the subcontractor card shows 'Action Required' and a red 'missing' chip even though the document is on file.
impact: A present, valid document is reported as missing — supervisors chase contractors for docs already supplied, and the expired/expiring banner counts are misleading for any doc type that legitimately has no expiry.
fixSketch: Distinguish 'no document on file' from 'document present, no expiry'. When a row exists with a dropbox_path/file but null expiry, compute status as 'current' (or a dedicated 'no_expiry' state) rather than 'missing'. 'missing' should mean the document type was never supplied, not 'supplied without an expiry date'.

title: Carpentry job/summary/budget/costs API leaks $ (cost & margin) to cost-stripped supervisors — UI strip only, server sends everything
evidence: GET list: `app.get("/api/carpentry/jobs", requireAuth, ...)` then `.from("carpentry_jobs").select("*")` → `ok(res, { jobs: rowsToCamel(data) })` (carpentryRoutes.mjs:203-220). GET detail: `.select("*")` → `rowToCamel(job)` (:346-380). GET summary (:1445-1509) returns `{ revenue, budgetCost, budgetMarginPct, labourActual, otherActual, totalActual, forecastMarginPct, variance }`. carpentry_jobs columns include `quoted_value ... ex-GST contract value`, `quoted_cost ... budgeted cost`, `quoted_margin_pct` (migration 065_carpentry_module.sql:36-38). The whole `/api/carpentry` prefix is gated admin+supervisor only (dev-api.mjs:851 `app.use("/api/carpentry", requireAuth, requireRole("admin", "supervisor"))`); none of these read routes add an admin-only gate. The frontend cost-strips DISPLAY only: FieldJobs.jsx:74 `{showCost && j.quotedValue != null && (...Quoted $...)}` with `showCost = can.viewCostData(role)` (= admin only, roles.js:40); CarpentryJobDetail.jsx:1734-1735 hides the budget/costs TABS with `visibleTabs = TABS.filter((t) => showCost || (t.id !== "budget" && t.id !== "costs"))`. repro: Log in as a supervisor. Open the field app → Jobs (/field/jobs) and tap any job (links to /carpentry/:jobId, which RoleRoute allows supervisor — App.jsx:307). The page hides the dollar tabs, but in DevTools → Network the response to GET /api/carpentry/jobs/:id contains quotedValue/quotedCost/quotedMarginPct, and a direct GET /api/carpentry/jobs/:id/summary (no admin gate) returns budgetMarginPct + forecastMarginPct + variance. Supervisors/leading hands can read builder cost, contract value and profit margin on every carpentry job — exactly the data the role is designed never to see. The protection is UI-only and trivially bypassed.
fixSketch: Strip cost fields server-side based on req.caller.role. In the carpentry list/detail handlers, after rowToCamel, if role !== 'admin' delete quotedValue/quotedCost/quotedMarginPct (and final_revenue/budget_margin_pct from any performance snapshot). Gate /summary, /budget, /costs, /budget/seed read+write with requireRole('admin') (or return a cost-free shape for supervisors). Mirror the client-portal cost-leak scan (docs/qa) to cover the supervisor role, not just clients.

title: FieldTasks/FieldDiary/FieldWHS load has no catch — a rejected Supabase fetch leaves the loading spinner stuck forever
evidence: FieldTasks.load() (FieldTasks.jsx:18-30): `const [{data: tasks},{data: projects}] = await Promise.all([...]); ... setLoading(false);` with NO try/catch — `setLoading(false)` is the last line, only reached if the await resolves. FieldDiary.jsx:28-34 `getSupabase().from('projects')...then(({data}) => { ...; setLoading(false); })` and FieldWHS.jsx:12-13 `...then(({data}) => { setProjects(data||[]); setLoading(false); })` both have no `.catch()`. Contrast FieldHome.jsx:22-51 which correctly wraps the same pattern in try/catch/finally so the spinner always clears.
repro: On a field device with flaky reception (or mid-token-refresh / CORS preflight failure), the Supabase REST fetch underlying these queries rejects rather than resolving. Open /field/tasks (or /diary, /whs): load() rejects → the trailing setLoading(false) never runs → `if (loading) return <Loading .../>` renders permanently. The page is a dead end until full reload; on the same conditions FieldHome recovers and shows its empty state.
impact: Permanent loading spinner / unusable page for a site worker on poor connectivity — the same failure mode as the supabaseConfigured-mount bug (load promise rejects, spinner never clears). Field app is mobile-first, so flaky networks are the common case, not the edge case.
fixSketch: Wrap each loader in try/catch/finally with `finally { setLoading(false); }` (copy FieldHome's structure), and surface a retry/error state. For FieldDiary/FieldWHS add `.catch(() => setLoading(false))` (or convert to async/await with try/finally).

title: Editing template content in the Hub silently reverts admin-edited metadata (status/title/purpose/category/module) to catalog defaults
repro: 1. Admin PATCHes a template's metadata, e.g. `PATCH /api/templates/progress-claim-email {"status":"archived","purpose":"Custom wording — do not use the catalog blurb","category":"Internal"}` — creates/updates the DB row; the registry now shows status=archived and the custom purpose (DB wins on merge). 2. Later, anyone opens that same email template in the Hub editor and clicks 'Save to Dropbox' (PUT /content). 3. The PUT update overwrites status→'active' (entry.status), purpose→the catalog purpose, category→catalog category, title→catalog title, module→catalog module. The admin's archived state and custom purpose are gone, with no warning.
impact: Admin curation of the template registry is silently lost whenever the body of an editable (email_md / whs_markdown) template is saved through the Hub. An archived template can re-appear as active; a hand-tuned purpose/category reverts to boilerplate. Note the clobber is also inconsistent — PATCH-set `description` is NOT in the PUT payload so it survives, while status/title/purpose/category/module do not — which makes the data state hard to reason about.
fixSketch: Don't overwrite catalog-derived metadata on a content save. Either (a) on update, only set the fields the content edit truly owns: `{ storage_path: path, edit_method: ..., version: ..., updated_at: ... }` (and on first insert, seed module/title/kind from entry but never overwrite them again), or (b) merge: read the existing row first and only fall back to `entry.*` for columns that are null in the DB. The version-bump and Dropbox write are correct; just stop the metadata overwrite.

title: Client can view internal/defect site photos — v2 media route and Home feed bypass the migration-110 client_visible flag
evidence: Media route serves bytes with NO visibility check: `.from("project_photos").select("storage_path, project_id").eq("id", photoId)... if (!photo || photo.project_id !== projectId) return res.status(404)... const buf = await dropboxDownloadBuffer(accessToken, photo.storage_path); return res.send(buf);` — it checks project membership and that the photo is in this project, but never checks `client_visible`. Home returns private photo IDs/captions: `.from("project_photos").select("id, caption, taken_at, is_hero").eq("project_id", projectId).order("taken_at"...).limit(8)` — again no `.eq("client_visible", true)`. Contrast the Journey route at :992-997 which DOES filter `.eq("client_visible", true)`. Migration 110 (110_portal_dispute_and_photo_visibility.sql:7-9,23-24) added `client_visible boolean DEFAULT false` precisely because 'project_photos has NO client-visibility flag, so the moment any photo gets a matching milestone_key it shows on the client's Journey UNCONDITIONALLY — including a defect photo a staffer buckets to a stage. Default to PRIVATE.'
repro: 1. Staff upload a defect/internal photo to a project (project_photos row, client_visible left at its default false). 2. Logged-in client opens Home: GET /api/portal/app/:projectId/home returns that photo's {id, caption} in recentPhotos (caption leak alone may disclose 'crack in slab', 'rework required', etc.). 3. Client requests GET /api/portal/app/:projectId/media/:photoId with that id (or any photo id on their project) and receives the full image bytes — even though client_visible=false.
impact: Defeats the entire purpose of migration 110. Clients can see internal/defect/QA photos and their captions that staff never marked visible — a dispute and reputational risk (a client seeing a defect photo the builder intended to fix before disclosure), and disclosure of internal site documentation. It is within-tenant (own project) but crosses the staff-controlled visibility boundary.
fixSketch: Add `.eq("client_visible", true)` to the media-route SELECT (return 404 if not client-visible) and to the Home recentPhotos query, mirroring the Journey route at :996. (Apply tolerantly if a DB may predate migration 110, but default-deny.)

title: Selection sign-off allows non-contractual invitees (architect/accountant) to make a binding, cost-impacting selection
lens: Authorization / role bypass on a financial action
evidence: `app.post(`${base}/selections/:selectionId/select`, requirePortalLogin, async (req, res) => {` — guarded by requirePortalLogin only, NOT requirePortalWrite. The handler then writes cost_impact (= option.price_inc_gst − selection.allowance_amount), sets status 'in_review', records an immutable audit 'selection.chosen', and clears the client_action. requirePortalWrite (requirePortalAuth.mjs:164-172) is the gate that enforces: 'only the primary/secondary client may take CONTRACTUAL actions. architect / accountant invitees have view access but cannot approve variations, notify payment, etc.' requirePortalLogin (requirePortalAuth.mjs:128-138) only checks isAuthenticated, so any active project_client_users member passes. Roles include 'architect' and 'accountant' (migration 103_client_portal_v2.sql:40-41 CHECK (role IN ('primary','secondary','architect','accountant'))).
repro: Invite an architect (role='architect', is_active=true) to a project. Logged in as that user: POST /api/portal/app/:projectId/selections/:selectionId/select {optionId} succeeds — recording a product choice with a cost delta against the contract, even though the documented intent restricts contractual choices to primary/secondary.
impact: A view-only invitee can commit the client to a selection that carries a cost impact (over/under allowance) and is treated as the client's decision in the audit trail and My Actions. Violates the stated contractual-action role policy; could trigger a supplier order based on an unauthorised party's choice.
fixSketch: Change the guard to `requirePortalWrite` (as the variation respond and payment-notify routes already use), or add an explicit `['primary','secondary'].includes(session.role)` check. Keep requirePortalLogin only on genuinely non-contractual actions.

title: Diary→Journey seed INSERT throws pre-migration-103 (no draft row is ever created), not merely orphaned
evidence:
syncDiaryToPortalUpdate inserts a row that includes a status column:
```
await sb.from("portal_updates").insert({
  project_id: projectId,
  week_of: weekOf,
  headline: `Site update — ${weekOf}`,
  body,
  author_name: entry.supervisor || "Site team",
  published: false,
  status: "draft"
});
```
But portal_updates in migration 027 (027_client_portal.sql:11-20) has NO status column — only id, project_id, week_of, headline, body, author_name, published, created_at. The status column (CHECK IN ('draft','reviewed','published')) is added only by migration 103 (103_client_portal_v2.sql:263-264), which per project memory is NOT applied to the live DB (live stops at 102). supabase-js rejects an insert that references a non-existent column (PGRST204), and the whole call is wrapped in try/catch that only console.warns (portalIntegration.mjs:536-538), so the failure is swallowed.
repro: On the live DB (migrations applied through 102), a supervisor saves a site diary entry with work_completed text → siteDiaryRoutes.mjs:100 calls syncDiaryToPortalUpdate → the portal_updates INSERT references the absent status column → PGRST204 thrown → caught + warned → zero rows written. No draft is created at all.
impact: The cohesion audit (Lane 9, line 173) characterises this as 'an orphaned row no UI publishes' — implying a row exists that a publish endpoint could later surface. In the actual live migration state the failure mode is harder: nothing is written, so any future 'load existing diary drafts to publish' UI (the audit's B3 fix) would find nothing to load for entries created before 103 is applied. Also means the existing UPDATE-only branch (line 523, refreshing a draft) can never run, because the initial INSERT that would create the draft always fails pre-103.
fixSketch: Either gate the status field behind a feature/migration check, or split the write like syncClaimPaid does (insert the always-existing columns first, then a best-effort separate update for status). Cleanest: apply migration 103 (it is the root gate the audit's B1 already calls out) and confirm portal_updates.status exists before relying on this path.

title: "Approved variation $" is defined three inconsistent ways → client and staff see different contract totals
repro: Finance issues a $40k variation (status='sent_to_client'). Client logs into v2 portal and clicks Approve → portal_decisions.status='approved', job_variations.status stays 'sent_to_client'. Now: (a) v2 portal Home/snapshot shows the $40k inside approvedVariations and a contract total raised by $44k inc-GST; (b) Finance command-centre dashboard for the same job shows that $40k in unsignedVar and the contract total UNCHANGED; (c) if this project were non-v2, the legacy /budget would also show it as pending. Client and builder are looking at different contract totals for the same variation until the builder manually signs in Finance.
impact: A money-confusion dispute vector — the exact class the v2 code comment at line 1163-1166 was trying to avoid, but it created a NEW divergence with the staff-facing Finance numbers instead. The client believes the contract is $44k higher and committed; Finance still treats it as a pending/unsigned (non-contractual) change. There is no single source of truth for 'current approved contract value' across the client and staff surfaces.
fixSketch: Pick one definition of 'approved variation' and apply it on both sides. Option A: have the Finance command-centre also treat a client-approved portal_decision as 'committed/approved' (mirror the v2 reconciliation against portal_decisions). Option B: keep canonical job_variations.status as the only source of truth and have the v2 snapshot show client-approved-not-signed as a distinct 'awaiting builder signature' bucket rather than folding it into approvedVariations/currentContractTotal. Either way, label it identically on client and staff dashboards.

title: Unauthenticated cron endpoints send emails to subcontractors (spam / reputation abuse)
evidence: app.post("/api/cron/rfq-reminders", async (_req, res) => { ... await runDeadlineReminders({ daysBefore: days }); ...}) and app.post("/api/cron/lead-time-notifications", async (req, res) => { const simulateDate = req.body?.simulateDate?.trim?.() || undefined; const result = await runLeadTimeNotifications(sb, { simulateDate }); ...}). Neither has requireAuth, requireRole, nor a CRON_SECRET check. runDeadlineReminders (server/lib/rfqReminders.mjs:76 `await sendPlainMail({ to, subject, text })`) and runLeadTimeNotifications (server/lib/scheduleReminders.mjs imports sendPlainMail and emails subcontractors) both actually send mail.
repro: From anywhere on the internet: `curl -X POST https://<api-host>/api/cron/rfq-reminders` → fires reminder emails to every subcontractor with an RFQ near deadline. `curl -X POST https://<api-host>/api/cron/lead-time-notifications -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"simulateDate":"2026-12-31"}'` → lets the attacker pick a date and trigger lead-time notification emails. No token required.
impact: Anonymous attacker can repeatedly trigger outbound email blasts to the company's subcontractor list, harming sender reputation/deliverability and spamming partners; the simulateDate param gives control over which notifications fire. The sibling cron routes /api/cron/portal-sync (1603) and /api/cron/cost-insights (1617) DO guard with CRON_SECRET, proving the omission here is an oversight, not intent.
fixSketch: Add the same CRON_SECRET guard used by portal-sync/cost-insights to both rfq-reminders and lead-time-notifications (reject unless req.headers['x-cron-secret']===process.env.CRON_SECRET). Better: factor a requireCronSecret middleware and apply it to every /api/cron/* route via a prefix app.use.

title: Unauthenticated company IMAP inbox reader
evidence: app.get("/api/mail/inbox", async (req, res) => { const cfg = imapConfig(); ... await client.connect(); await client.mailboxOpen("INBOX"); ... for await (const msg of client.fetch(...)) }) — no requireAuth on the route.
repro: `curl https://<api-host>/api/mail/inbox?limit=50` with no Authorization header returns the most recent inbox messages (envelopes: from, subject, date, and parsed content) for the IMAP account configured via IMAP_USER (the company invoice/quote inbox).
impact: Any anonymous caller reads the company's real email inbox — supplier invoices, quotes, client correspondence, PII. Confidentiality breach of the most sensitive mailbox in the business.
fixSketch: Add requireAuth (and likely requireRole('admin')) to /api/mail/inbox. It is a staff-only finance/tender tool.

title: Carpentry cost/budget endpoints leak dollar figures to the supervisor role (cost-stripped role bypass)
evidence: Prefix gate: app.use("/api/carpentry", requireAuth, requireRole("admin", "supervisor")) (dev-api.mjs:851). The budget route returns full money: ok(res, { lines, totals, burn }) where lines carry {budget, actual, variance} and totals carry {labourBudget, labourActual, totalActual} and burn carries {teamChargeUpPerDay, teamBreakEvenPerDay, labourMarginRemaining} (carpentryRoutes.mjs:1394-1436). /costs (1189) and /summary (1445) similarly expose $ . But roles.js declares viewCostData: (r) => r === "admin" and the UI enforces it: CarpentryJobDetail.jsx:1734 `const showCost = can.viewCostData(role)` then 1735 hides the Budget/Costs tabs for supervisors.
repro: Log in as a supervisor (passes requireRole('admin','supervisor')). The UI hides the Budget/Costs tabs, but `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <supervisor_jwt>' https://<api-host>/api/carpentry/jobs/<id>/budget` returns budget/actual/variance/charge-up-rate/margin dollars.
impact: A supervisor — explicitly a cost-stripped field role per roles.js and ROLE_DESCRIPTIONS ('no finance, sales, marketing or cost figures') — can read job cost, margin, pay-rate-derived charge-up and break-even figures directly from the API, contradicting the project's cost-data law. Frontend gating exists with no matching backend gate.
fixSketch: Add requireRole('admin') to the carpentry cost surfaces specifically: /api/carpentry/jobs/:id/budget, /budget/seed, /costs (GET+POST), and strip $ from /summary for non-admins (return cost fields only when req.caller.role==='admin'). Do not rely on the admin+supervisor prefix gate for money.

title: Unauthenticated Dropbox upload/folder-creation routes (write to company file store)
evidence: app.post("/api/dropbox/ensure-job-folders", async ...), app.post("/api/dropbox/upload-tender-document", async ...) (accepts dataBase64 → Buffer.from(...,'base64') → uploadTenderDocumentToJob), app.post("/api/dropbox/save-rfq-email-copy", ...), app.post("/api/dropbox/save-quote-pdf", ...). None has requireAuth, and /api/dropbox is not in the prefix-gate loop at line 835.
repro: `curl -X POST https://<api-host>/api/dropbox/upload-tender-document -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"jobAddress":"<any address>","fileName":"x.pdf","dataBase64":"<base64>"}'` with no token writes an arbitrary file into the company's Dropbox job folder; ensure-job-folders creates arbitrary folder trees.
impact: Anonymous attacker can write arbitrary files (including malicious payloads disguised as quotes/tender docs) into the company's shared Dropbox namespace and pollute the folder structure. These files are surfaced to staff as legitimate job documents.
fixSketch: Add requireAuth to all four /api/dropbox/* routes (these are staff upload actions). Optionally add a /api/dropbox prefix gate in the loop. Validate jobAddress against an existing job.

title: Unauthenticated AI re-extract endpoint mutates RFQ rows and burns paid Claude/Dropbox calls
evidence: app.post("/api/rfq/:rfqId/reextract-amount", async (req, res) => { ... pdfBuffer = await dropboxDownloadSharedLink(...); ... const extraction = await extractQuoteFromPdf(pdfBuffer, ...); ... await sb.from("rfqs").update({ ... }).eq("id", req.params.rfqId) }) — no requireAuth. Compare the sibling /api/rfq/extract (1199), /api/rfq/send (1873), /api/rfq/remind-one (1831) which all carry requireAuth.
repro: `curl -X POST https://<api-host>/api/rfq/<rfqId>/reextract-amount` with no token downloads the quote PDF from Dropbox, calls the paid Claude API, and overwrites rfqs.quoted_amount/quote_extraction for that RFQ.
impact: Anonymous write to financial RFQ data (quoted_amount feeds tender comparisons) plus cost abuse of paid Anthropic + Dropbox APIs. Inconsistent with every other /api/rfq/* route which is requireAuth-gated.
fixSketch: Add requireAuth (this is a tender-manager action; admin per the broader tender surface). Match the gating on /api/rfq/extract and /api/rfq/send.

title: Unauthenticated Blueprint AI endpoints (paid-API abuse, no auth)
evidence: app.post('/api/blueprint/review-document', async ...) calls callAI(getAnthropic(), {model: MODEL, max_tokens: MAX_TOKENS, ...}); app.post('/api/blueprint/generate-sop', async ...) → callClaude('sop', messages); app.post('/api/blueprint/troubleshoot', async ...) → callClaude('troubleshoot', messages). None has requireAuth, whereas the sibling /api/blueprint/chat (325) and /chat/stream (277) DO carry requireAuth. (/api/blueprint/learn at 397 is at least protected by requireLearnAccess via BLUEPRINT_LEARN_KEY — but only in production: blueprintRoutes.mjs:254 returns true when NODE_ENV!=='production' and no key set.)

title: Unauthenticated read of unmatched quote emails (PII / correspondence leak)
evidence: app.get("/api/quote-tracker/unmatched", async (_req, res) => { ... sb.from("unmatched_quote_emails").select("*").is("resolved_at", null)... return res.json({ ok: true, serviceConfigured: true, items: data || [] }) }) — no requireAuth. The matching write, /api/unmatched-quotes/resolve (jobsApiRoutes.mjs:206), IS requireAuth-gated.
repro: `curl https://<api-host>/api/quote-tracker/unmatched` with no token returns up to 100 unmatched inbound emails including from_email, subject, and body_preview.
impact: Anonymous disclosure of inbound email metadata/content (sender addresses, subjects, body previews) harvested from the IMAP poller. Privacy/confidentiality leak.

title: Double-GST cost booking: Buildexact material push falls back to inc-GST amount_total as the ex-GST unit cost
evidence: const amount = Number(doc.amount_ex_gst || doc.amount_total || 0);  ...  items: [{ costItemType: "Material", ... unitCost: amount, totalCost: amount ... }]  with createPurchaseOrder({ ..., isTaxFree: false, ... }) at line 597. amount_total is the GST-INCLUSIVE grand total (parser line 358: matches TOTAL/Amount Due/Balance Due; LLM prompt line ~398 defines amount_total as the full total). amount_ex_gst is only the subtotal and is frequently null. With isTaxFree:false, Buildexact applies 10% GST ON TOP of the figure passed as unitCost — so an inc-GST $1,100 invoice is pushed as a $1,100 ex-GST cost and booked as $1,210 actual cost.
repro: 1. Drop/IMAP-ingest a supplier RECEIPT that shows only a 'TOTAL $1,100.00' line — no 'Subtotal'/'Ex GST' line and the words 'tax invoice' absent (common for EFTPOS receipts / hardware-store dockets). 2. Parser: gstM/exM don't match → gst_amount=null, amount_ex_gst=null; totalM matches → amount_total=1100. The derivation block (financeRoutes.mjs:365-373) only fills amount_ex_gst when gst_amount exists, and the 1/11 rule (line 370) only fires when /tax invoice/i matches — so amount_ex_gst stays null. Stored as-is (lines 782-784). 3. Approve the doc on a carpentry job linked to Buildexact → pushMaterialInvoiceToBuildexact runs → amount=doc.amount_total=1100 → PO line unitCost=1100, isTaxFree:false → Buildexact records $1,210 actual cost.
impact: Actual material cost overstated by 10% on every receipt-style invoice that lacks an explicit ex-GST subtotal line. Inflates committed/actual cost, understates job margin (the very metric Finance uses for go/no-go and the -margin alerts), and makes the Buildexact reconciliation (buildexactReconcile.mjs) drift. Silent — no error surfaced.
fixSketch: Never feed an inc-GST figure into an isTaxFree:false line. Either (a) require/derive a true ex-GST value before push: const ex = doc.amount_ex_gst ?? (doc.amount_total != null ? exGst(doc.amount_total) : null); refuse the push if ex==null; or (b) when only amount_total is known, push with the GST already inside and set isTaxFree:true. Use exGst()/GST_RATE from constants.js, and guarantee at ingest that amount_ex_gst is always populated (extend the derivation block to: if amount_total && !amount_ex_gst → amount_ex_gst = round(amount_total/(1+GST_RATE))).

title: Actuals undercount: normalized-cost rollup sums only amount_ex_gst, dropping invoices that only carry amount_total
evidence: const { data: approved } = await sb2.from("financial_documents").select("amount_ex_gst").eq("job_id", doc.job_id).eq("trade_category_id", doc.trade_category_id).in("status", [...]);  const totalActual = (approved || []).reduce((s, d) => s + Number(d.amount_ex_gst || 0), 0);  — any approved doc whose amount_ex_gst is null (same data condition as finding #1) contributes 0 to the trade's actual cost.
repro: Same receipt-style invoice as finding #1 (amount_ex_gst=null, amount_total=1100). Approve it → upsertNormalizedCost is called with a totalActual that EXCLUDES the $1,100 entirely (treated as $0).
impact: The same null-ex-GST invoice that finding #1 OVER-books into Buildexact (+10%) is here UNDER-booked into the Hub's normalized_costs (as $0). The two cost views contradict each other for the identical document. Cost-intelligence / job-budget actuals silently omit cash-receipt spend, overstating remaining budget and margin.
fixSketch: Roll up on a guaranteed-populated ex-GST value: select amount_ex_gst, amount_total and use Number(d.amount_ex_gst ?? exGst(d.amount_total) ?? 0). Better, enforce at ingest that amount_ex_gst is always derived from amount_total (see finding #1 fix) so every consumer can rely on it. Import exGst from constants.js.
